LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch the 'Thursday Night Football' matchup, plus a preview and prediction Patrick Smith/Getty Images In the Week 10 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the New York Giants play host to the division rival Washington Commanders . New York enters this game riding high atop the NFC East, having won each of its last two games sandwiching a Week 8 bye. The Giants are surprisingly in the playoff picture in the first year of the John Harbaugh era despite losing starting quarterback Jaxson Dart in Week 2. They recently turned to J.J. McCarthy in place of Jameis Winston but kept on winning. Washington climbed out of last place in the NFC East thanks to a Week 8 win over the lowly Philadelphia Eagles but still has the second-worst record in the conference. The Commanders missed an opportunity for a win the last time these two teams played by mismanaging the clock as poorly as any team ever has, and they will surely be looking to atone for that mistake here. Will the Giants keep rolling, or will the Commanders capture a rare victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Giants vs. Commanders live Date: Thursday, Nov. 12 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: MetLife Stadium (East Rutherford, New Jersey) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Giants -2.5, O/U 40.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Commanders have the ball The Commanders are not particularly effective either passing or running the football. They rank 21st in the NFL in net yards per pass attempt (which accounts for yards lost to sacks), and they're 23rd in designed rushing yards per carry, which eliminates scrambling from the picture. Their most effective form of offense is scrambling, where Jayden Daniels and Marcus Mariota have run 29 times for 274 yards — the most scramble yards in the NFL, per Tru Media. But that's not something that you can lean on down-to-down. Daniels has completed only 63.9% of his passes at an average of 6.9 yards per attempt. While he has seven passing touchdowns and has yet to be intercepted, he has a low passing success rate (43.9%, according to Tru Media), has generated explosives at only an average rate (7.8%) and has struggled on third downs (30.9%). Again, his most effective way of moving the ball has been via the scramble. The Giants are actually second in the NFL in passing success rate allowed and third in explosives per dropback, according to Tru Media. So Daniels, with his limited receiving corps in the absence of Terry McLaurin , might find it difficult to move the ball through the air. The Giants, though, have been vulnerable to opponent scrambles, allowing quarterbacks to take off downfield on a league-high 23.9% of pressured dropbacks and yielding 225 scramble yards to date. So Daniels could have some room to run. In the absence of Jacory Croskey-Merritt , the Commies have turned to Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler in the backfield. They have not been particularly effective on the ground, but they're each capable outlet receivers for Daniels, who has targeted backs on 14.4% of his passes, a slightly higher rate than last year (12.8%). Doing so against the Giants may not be the most advisable strategy, though, because it means testing rookie linebacker Arvell Reese in space, and Reese has been a space-eating demon so far this season. Daniels' other pass-catchers at the moment are Stefon Diggs , Antonio Williams , Van Jefferson and Chig Okonkwo. The Giants have been good at limiting tight ends over the middle (there's Reese showing up again), so the passing game might run through the perimeter receivers, who will face off with an improved Deonte Banks and the recently-extended Greg Newsome II on the outside. Look for Daniels to at least try to test those guys deep down the field, given he has the seventh-highest deep throw rate among qualified quarterbacks. The Giants have faced deep passes at essentially an average rate so far this season, and they've been excellent at defending them, checking in second in EPA per dropback on those plays. Still, dinking and dunking hasn't been all that effective for Daniels and the Commanders, so they're going to have to try to hit on a few big plays. When the Giants have the ball The Giants turned to J.J. McCarthy as their quarterback in garbage time of their loss to the Saints back in Week 6, and they have stuck with him over the last two games. They've been a somewhat unusual offense with McCarthy under center. McCarthy himself has not been efficient on a down-to-down basis. He's completed only 63.2% of his passes, and he has one touchdown pass and one interception. He checks in 31st in success rate among 37 quarterbacks with at least 75 dropbacks this season, according to Tru Media. But McCarthy is averaging 9.1 (!!!!) yards per attempt, and he's 15th among the same group of 37 quarterbacks in EPA per dropback. That's because when he does complete passes, they're basically all going for big gains in big situations. He's throwing the ball farther downfield than anyone in the league (10.6-yard average depth of target), and he's leading the NFL in explosive plays per dropback at 16.0%, per Tru Media. The Commanders' defense is essentially the opposite of what McCarthy has done so far. They yield a high passing success rate (21st in the league) but a low explosive rate (11th). The tension between those two poles will be interesting to watch play out on Monday night. When McCarthy drops back to pass, he is looking most often to Malik Nabers , who has been the intended receiver on 31.7% of McCarthy's throws. Malachi Fields , not Isaiah Likely , has been the secondary target, with a 20.6% target share compared to Likely's 17.5% rate. Before McCarthy took over at quarterback, Likely tied Nabers for the team lead in target share at 29.4%, compared to just 11.2% for Fields. Nabers and Fields will do most of their work against Rasul Douglas and Amik Robertson on the outside, while Likely will see a lot of rookie linebacker Sonny Styles , slot corner Mike Sainristil and safeties Jeremy Reaves and Nick Cross . The Commanders have not generated very much pressure this season (33.5% of opponent dropbacks, per Tru Media, 25th in the league), while McCarthy has been one of the league's most-pressured quarterbacks since taking over. He tends to hold the ball for a while as he looks to push it down the field. Whether the Commanders can get after him will go a long way toward determining whether he can complete any big plays. Cam Skattebo is back for the Giants in this game, and he's likely to take over the lead role from Devin Singletary , who struggled last week and is more suited to being a passing-down back. Skattebo hasn't been very effective as a rusher this season, averaging 4.3 yards per carry with a 45.9% success rate, but he had his best game of the year before sitting out last week after the bye. The Commanders have been solid against the run, yielding only 3.9 yards per carry, with below-average marks both before (1.09) and after contact (2.83). This might be a game where the Giants lean on those big plays from McCarthy. I don't feel particularly comfortable predicting that this Giants team will improve to 6-2-1, but I just don't have much faith this version of Washington can be all that competitive either. The Commanders can't run the ball right now and have to lean on a passing game that hasn't been all that efficient. The Giants haven't exactly looked like world beaters this year (four of their five wins have come in one-score games), and they definitely didn't look great against the Eagles last week, but I think they can get it done on Thursday night. TOP Pick Commanders vs Giants prediction: Commanders +2.5 The Washington Commanders aren't as bad as their 2-5-1 record might lead you to believe, and the New York Giants aren't as good as their 5-2-1 record might indicate. Washington went down to the wire with the Rams in Week 9, losing a close game while gaining more yards per play than L.A. Two games before that, the Commanders lost by six in San Francisco, but were competitive enough to cover the spread. They've shown plenty of fight against good competition and tied these Giants in Week 5 , but probably should've won after winning the yards-per-play battle 6.3 to 4.9 . Wet, chilly weather is expected, which could make Washington's biggest advantage even more important: the ground game. It ranks eighth in yards per rush against a Giants defense ranked 27th in yards per rush allowed . Throw in a sketchy quarterback situation, with J.J. Both defenses are awful in the red zone, with the Giants dead last in opponent red-zone touchdown conversion percentage and the Commanders at 29th. Expect touchdowns, not field goal attempts, if they get in close, which helps support the Over on this low total. Don't forget these teams combined for 54 points in that Week 5 matchup. Bringing it all together is a Washington defense that's allowed eight touchdowns to tight ends in eight games, and Isaiah Likely leads New York in TD catches. That's a pretty significant gap, considering Ekeler actually had one more touch than White against the Rams last week. With their workloads this close, and New York a disaster in the red zone, I'll gladly take the bigger payout. Who wll win this time? | Getty Images Ed Valentine · SB Nation Thu, November 12, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Giants and Washington Commanders kick off Week 10 of the NFL season Thursday night at what promises to be a rainy, chilly MetLife Stadium. Can the Giants solidify their NFC East lead, or will the race for the division title tighten? Here is how the Big Blue View staff sees that game, and the rest of the Week 10 matchups. Which version of the Giants will show up on Thursday night? Will we get the sloppy Giants that came out flat against the Philadelphia Eagles, or the tough, physical, and technically sound Giants that showed up against the Houston Texans? John Harbaugh's 9-1 record home record on Thursday Nights is encouraging. I would say that this is a game the Giants should win on paper, particularly with Washington missing some of their best players and their starting center in the concussion protocol. However, I'm also not convinced that these Giants can play a normal game and just take care of business. I keep waiting for the Giants to play a complete game and execute on offense and defense, but this team seems unable to be both consistent and explosive. I hope the offensive line comes prepared to bully an injured Washington defensive line and J.J. McCarthy isn't forced into low percentage throws every third down by long yardage situations. Likewise, I hope that Dennard Wilson comes out swinging on defense, but also has a counterpunch ready in case Jayden Daniels has an answer to the Cover-0 blitz. I'm picking the Giants here, but they can't afford to take Washington lightly or give Jayden Daniels the chance to catch his breath and swing the game. Tony Del Genio This is the Giants' second consecutive must-win game. You wouldn't think that when 5-2-1 plays 2-5-1, but (1) the Giants haven't beaten the Commanders since Jayden Daniels became their quarterback (even though Daniels didn't play in one of those losses), (2) despite their record, Washington has beaten the Seahawks and only narrowly lost to the 49ers and Rams while the Giants were beaten soundly by the Rams, the only good team they've faced, and still have the 49ers and Seahawks coming up, along with the Jaguars and Lions. A division loss greatly weakens their hold on the NFC East lead, their only real path to the playoffs. Terry McLaurin is out for the season, but in his place is Stefon Diggs, who did not face the Giants in the first game. Jacory Crosky-Merritt, who beat the Giants' run D for a 33-yard TD right off the bat in the first game, is also out. The Commanders are further decimated by injuries since their last meeting to key starters such as DT Daron Payne and IOL Lucas Patrick. So really the Giants should prevail. The problem is…containing the running of Daniels, which they did not do well in their first meeting (103 yards, by far his highest of the season, and his only 2 rushing TDs of the season). Hopefully Dennard Wilson will have a plan for that. If so, and if the Giants execute it, then the Giants can win. David Hartman The rematch of the NFL's only tie game of the season will be played in prime time on Thursday night, and for the ninth time in nine games, the Giants are playing a team that doesn't have a winning record. But you can throw the records out the window: The 5-2-1 Giants, at home, are just 1.5 point favorites over the 2-5-1 Commanders. Go figure… Big Blue won with defense and a strong kicking game on Sunday in Philadelphia, with Arvel Reese perhaps becoming a star in real time. It was an ugly win, with the offense producing just 19 points. The Giants will need more than that against Jayden Daniels and company on Thursday night. Cam Skattebo is expected back, and that's good news. New York couldn't run the ball on Sunday, which stagnated their offense. Right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) might miss this game, however, and the O-line struggled at Philadelphia as it was. J.J. McCarthy wasn't terrible on Sunday, but he wasn't especially good either and now he's dealing with a hip pointer. Jameis Winston led New York on its only touchdown drive while McCarthy was temporarily knocked from the game. McCarthy hasn't thrown a TD pass (or an interception) in either of his two starts. This figures to be a close game, just like the first one. It'll be fun to watch standout rookies Reese and Sonny Styles — college teammates at Ohio State last season — leading the way for each defense. Seriously – how did anyone score on the Buckeyes? Anyway, Dennard Wilson needs to find a way to keep Daniels from gashing his defense with his legs. He ran for 103 yards and two scores in the first game. This game could come down to intangibles like turnovers and special teams. The G-Men have been winning (or tying) close games and that's a reflection on good coaching to a degree, and favorable luck. In a game that should be close, who am I to pick against that? Pick: Giants in a squeaker Valentine's View We are not picking games by the spread here, but I am surprised the Giants are just 1.5-point favorites. That indicates a continuing lack of real belief in the Giants in the betting market. The Giants understand the opportunity they have in front of them, and how important this game is. In the rainy, windy, miserable conditions at MetLife Stadium Thursday evening I think you have to expect what has become a typical Giants game this season — close, somewhat sloppy, decided by who makes the plays and who properly handles the situations at the end of the game. I have far more faith in the Giants to do that than I do the Commanders. We all remember the Commanders stunning clock mismanagement at the end of the Week 5 tie with the Giants. That sort of questionable decision-making has continued to plague Washington, which is 1-3-1 in games decided by one score. If you could the Arizona game, which I do since it was decided on the game's final play, seven of the Giants eight games this season were one-score games. The Giants are 5-1-1 in those games. They have lived on the edge, and have shown an ability to survive. Is that formula sustainable forever? Maybe not. It does, though, make me feel good about the Giants' chances on Thursday. picks.headline: NFL Thursday Night Football preview: Commanders try to put previous nightmare vs. Giants behind them
picks.blurb: NFL Thursday Night Football preview: Commanders try to put previous nightmare vs. Giants behind them - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Commanders edge Giants Skattebo's spooky stare 'Who Let the Dogs Out'? It's official: Poch to Man United Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Frank Schwab Senior writer Thu, November 12, 2026 at 4:28 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Washington Commanders should have had a win over the New York Giants this season. Or at least a field-goal attempt for the win. The last time the Commanders and Giants played, it ended with one of the worst game-management fiascos in recent years. The Commanders were in line for a game-winning 42-yard field goal in overtime. Then it got weird. Washington was painfully slow in running a play from scrimmage in the final minute; Jayden Daniels inexplicably allowed himself to be tackled, and time ran out before Washington could spike it. The game ended in a tie with Washington never getting that field-goal attempt. Washington is 1-2 since then, and its record this season is a disappointing 2-5-1. The Giants, gifted a half-win in Washington, are 2-1 since then and 5-2-1 overall, good for first place in the NFC East. The Giants aren't a dominant team, but they're in a great position to win the division and host a playoff game. If the season ended now, they'd be the No. 3 seed in the NFC. Acquiring J.J. McCarthy for a fifth-round pick has had a big impact on their season (and the Vikings' season too). McCarthy isn't coming off his best game — Jameis Winston led the Giants' only touchdown drive in a 19-11 win over the Eagles last week — and is dealing with a hip pointer, but overall he has shown some promise. The Commanders have been a mess most of the season, and Daniels rightfully said after last week's loss to the Rams that the Giants game is a "must-win." They can't afford a loss. Or even a half-loss like they took when these teams met the first time. Washington Commanders head coach Dan Quinn looks on after his team tied the Giants in Week 5. (AP Photo/Nick Wass) Who needs it more? The Commanders' season is practically over, and Dan Quinn's job status might be in jeopardy with a loss on Thursday. If Washington loses, it would be four games behind the Giants and New York would own the tiebreaker. There wouldn't be much reason for hope if that happens. But if the Commanders win, they'd be just two games back and have the tiebreaker. That's a massive swing. The Giants want to get this win to practically eliminate the Commanders and move closer to an NFC East title, but Washington is clearly the more desperate team. Key player: Giants WR Malik Nabers Malik Nabers came into the season with some questions over his health, as he was coming off a torn ACL. But over the first half of the season, he has re-established himself as one of the top young receivers in the NFL. He has 53 catches for 648 yards, and that is after a pretty slow start. He had four 100-yard games in a row, a streak that was snapped last week. In the first meeting with the Commanders, Nabers had 11 catches for 121 yards and a game-tying touchdown with 1:43 left in regulation. The Commanders do not have a cornerback who can reasonably match up with Nabers. Washington is 30th in passing yards allowed and 28th in passing touchdowns allowed. If they can't contain Nabers, it could be a long night. Betting market watch The New York Giants have a sizable lead in the NFC East and have also been one of the most reliable teams for bettors to back this season (6-2 against the spread). It wasn't pretty, but J.J. McCarthy, Jameis Winston & Co. won (and covered) on Sunday against the Eagles. Although McCarthy left the game briefly with a hip injury, it appears he'll play. On the other sideline, the Commanders had yet another late-game blunder in a 20-13 loss to the Los Angeles Rams in Week 9. Washington is going nowhere fast, and the team has a lot more questions than answers at the moment. It's a little surprising this spread is only New York -2.5, but it's also hard not to back Big Blue at under a field goal. — Ben Fawkes Check out more of Ben's work at the Yahoo Sports betting hub . Fantasy football storylines The Giants and Commanders played an adorable tie game five weeks ago, with both teams frittering away a likely win in overtime. Thursday night, they get the anticipated rematch. Here are three fantasy themes to track as you watch the game. 1. Will Malik Nabers go off again? Nabers had a four-game streak of 100-yard efforts snapped last week, but this is a great chance to get cooking again. He drew 20 targets and posted an 11-121-1 return the last time he faced Washington's beatable secondary. 2. Can Jayden Daniels get his running mojo back? Daniels needs to run proactively to be at his best, and he gashed the Giants for 103 yards in that prior meeting. He's had just 49 yards rushing, total, in his last three starts. The Washington pass-catchers are ordinary, so if Daniels is going to be a fantasy-worthy start here, he needs to use his athleticism. 3. Is Cam Skattebo back in the Circle of Trust? It's been a whirlwind sophomore year for Skattebo — fumbles, injury, a soft benching. And the Giants did kick the tires on a Jonathan Taylor trade this week. Alas, Skattebo is someone they probably need, given how poorly Devin Singletary played against the Eagles. The Washington run defense has been solid all year, a stark contrast to the pass defense. — Scott Pianowski Check out more of Scott's work at the Yahoo Sports fantasy hub .

away.headline: Commanders-Rams final injury report rules out two receivers, leaves McDuffie questionable
away.blurb: The Washington Commanders released their final injury report Friday ahead of their matchup with the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday. The report listed two of Washington's receivers, Treylon Burks (foot) and Dyami Brown (calf), as officially OUT against the Rams. Burks missed practice all week with an injured foot that he's been dealing with since the 49ers game, while Brown was added to Thursday's report as limited before missing Friday's practice. With Terry McLaurin already out for the season, Washington will need more from Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams, who led the team with seven targets and five catches for 54 yards against Philadelphia . Van Jefferson could see more work, and Luke McCaffrey is another option. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn spoke Friday about Jefferson's readiness: "I liked his approach. I liked his readiness, and so when called upon, I'd expect he'd play well." Rookie Jaden Bradley could also be elevated from the practice squad, although Washington hasn't announced that move. Elsewhere on the report, Jer'Zhan Newton is questionable with his pectoral injury despite practicing fully all three days. Newton is still in his 21-day practice window and must be activated from injured reserve before he can play. That decision carries some weight with Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw now on IR . Shy Tuttle (shoulder) was limited all week but carries no game designation, while Sam Cosmi (knee) returned to full participation Friday. John Bates (shoulder) was limited throughout the week but has no game designation either. Los Angeles has some injury problems of its own, particularly in the secondary . Cornerback Jaylen Watson (shoulder) is out, while Trent McDuffie (back) is questionable after missing every practice this week. Former Commanders safety Kam Curl (foot) is also questionable after returning to limited practice Friday. The Rams could be short-handed in the secondary, although McDuffie's and Curl's availability won't be settled until closer to kickoff. The Rams also listed long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle) as doubtful, with tight end Colby Parkinson (ribs), linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring), and receiver Jordan Whittington (back) questionable. Quarterback Matthew Stafford practiced fully throughout the week, while head coach Sean McVay expects Myles Garrett to play Sunday, pending his activation from injured reserve. Tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) was ruled out after injuring his hamstring in Friday’s practice . The bad news is that the two injuries come from the offensive side of the ball. Center Lucas Patrick and tight end Colson Yankoff have been ruled out for the game , and it'll be next man up for the Commanders. Patrick was placed in the concussion protocol during their game last week against the Los Angeles Rams. As for Yankoff, he's dealing with a knee injury. With Patrick out, Nick Allegretti is expected to be the starting center for the matchup. It would be a good thing if Burks were able to suit up, especially with some of the injuries their receivers have had this season. home.headline: Commanders-Giants Final Injury Report: Lucas Patrick Out, Treylon Burks Expected Back Despite Missed Practice
home.blurb: Commanders-Giants Final Injury Report: Lucas Patrick Out, Treylon Burks Expected Back Despite Missed Practice Skip to main content SI.COM Lucas Patrick is out Thursday night against the New York Giants. The Commanders’ final injury report also ruled out tight end Colson Yankoff, leaving Washington to start Nick Allegretti at center in place of Patrick. Patrick entered concussion protocol during Sunday’s loss to the Rams, and rookie Matt Gulbin finished that game at center. Head coach Dan Quinn confirmed Tuesday that Allegretti will start against New York. Gulbin got the call Sunday because he had been taking the center reps while Allegretti worked at guard, a decision I wrote more about earlier this week . According to Washington's official website, the Giants blitz at the third-highest rate in the NFL. Allegretti will have to help set the protection against that defense with Jayden Daniels behind him. Treylon Burks missed Wednesday’s practice with the foot injury that kept him out against the Rams, but he has no game designation. Quinn said the day off was planned after Burks got work Tuesday and that the receiver was expected to be ready Thursday. Washington did not practice Monday and held a walkthrough Tuesday, so those first two participation reports were estimates. Burks’ place on the active list will be confirmed with Thursday’s inactives. Yankoff did not practice during the short week because of a knee injury. His absence reaches beyond the tight end rotation: Washington credited him with 185 special teams snaps this season. John Bates (shoulder) was full all three days, and Chig Okonkwo (hip) was full Tuesday and Wednesday. Neither has a game designation. Pick: Texans 21, Browns 20 Minnesota Vikings at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) The Packers are coming off an impressive road victory over the Patriots and Jordan Love has been on fire. The Patriots, which are off to a 5-4 start, are coming off a 45-27 defeat at the hands of Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers. Meanwhile, the Lions, which are sitting at 6-2, defeated the Miami Dolphins, 19-9, in their Week 9 tilt . New England – led by Mike Vrabel on the sidelines – has lost two of its last three games, including to the Chicago Bears in Week 7. Additionally, it sits basically in the middle of the pack in both points scored (23.4/game) and points allowed (23.0/g). Yet, the Patriots still possess a myriad of talent on both sides of the ball. On offense, they're led under center by third-year passer Drake Maye, who has thrown for 18 touchdowns, 2,282 yards and a league-high 11 interceptions through nine games. He's coming off a three-interception performance against the Packers in which he completed a season-low 55.3 percent of his passes. Maye's top target this year has been veteran tight end Hunter Henry, who has amassed 32 catches, 361 yards and two touchdowns through the season's first nine games. And on the ground, the Patriots are spearheaded by sixth-year back Rhamondre Stevenson. Stevenson, a fourth-round pick of New England, has accumulated 399 yards and two touchdowns, and is presently averaging 3.9 yards per carry. Then, on the defensive side of the ball, the Patriots have received strong performances this season from the likes of EDGE defenders Gabe Jacas and Elijah Ponder, cornerback Carlton Davis III and linebacker Christian Elliss. Ponder, a second-year pro , has already recorded 7.5 sacks, eight tackles for loss and 13 QB hits, and has returned a fumble for a touchdown. And for his efforts, he's earned a 75.0 overall grade from Pro Football Focus, the 23rd-best overall grade among 110 qualified players at the position. The Patriots will not, however, have the services of Davis (knee) for this Week 10 international affair. Plus, they will also be down starting left guard Ben Brown (knee), and are expected to be without Stevenson (knee). Stevenson, the team's No. 1 back, suffered a plantaris tendon tear last week against the Packers. Those are three significant losses for Vrabel's squad going into its matchup with Detroit. As for the Lions, they will also be down multiple starters in Week 10: linebacker Jack Campbell (neck), center Cade Mays (ankle) and cornerback D.J. Reed (hip). Plus, safety Kerby Joseph, who has yet to play a single game in 2026, will not be making his season debut in Germany. While both teams are rather significantly banged up, I still believe this matchup favors Detroit. At this present juncture, I believe the Lions have a 59 percent chance to secure their fifth straight victory. The Detroit Lions (6-2) are headed to Munich, Germany, to take on the New England Patriots (5-4) in an overseas edition of Week 10 NFL Football. It's been 11 seasons since the Lions last played an international game, but this trip has been in the works for some time. In 2024, as part of the NFL's Global Markets Program, the Lions have had marketing rights in the DACH region , which includes Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. Since then, the team has made several trips to Germany and has helped support Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown— whose mother, Miriam Brown, was born and raised in Germany —in running youth football programs across the country. As for the game itself, it looks like it'll be a good one, and the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -2.5 points . While the Lions are riding a four-game winning streak, the Patriots' 2026 season has been a more up-and-down affair after reaching the Super Bowl in 2025. They opened the season by losing to the Seahawks, beat the Steelers, then lost to the Jaguars over the first three weeks. They got back to 2-2 with a big win over the Bills, then rallied to 4-2 after wins over the Raiders and Jets. The Bears took them down on Thursday night in Week 7, but the Patriots eeked out a five-point win over the Dolphins to reach 5-3. On Sunday, the Patriots took on the Packers and looked completely unprepared. Packer QB Jordan Love jumped all over them, throwing for 372 yards and three scores, while Patriots Drake Maye threw for 299 yards and three scores, but also threw three interceptions and was sacked four times. On the ground, the Packers' worst-ranked rushing offense ran for 129 yards and two touchdowns, while the Pats gained 94 rushing yards, a touchdown, and lost a fumble. In the end, the Packers left Foxborough with a 45-27 win, and left former Patriots QB and current color commentator Tom Brady wondering who this New England team actually is: "Half the season they played like this, and the other half of the season they haven't turned the ball over, they haven't exposed the defense, have played more physical on defense, but right now it's just too inconsistent. Which team are they going to get? The team that is loose with the ball, is loose with decision-making, looking like they can be beaten by anybody. Or the team that takes care of the football, that makes the other team play left-handed, and can do what they want to do. Can they be a good team? They haven't quite done that because good teams leave the smallest margin of error." The Lions and Patriots are scheduled to play on Sunday, November 15, at 9:30 a.m. ET at Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany.

picks.blurb: 2. Not-so Super: The Patriots, just like many teams before them, haven't been able to escape the Super Bowl hangover this season. Injuries and inconsistencies are a big reason for that, but so is the drop-off in play from Drake Maye. He has already set a career-high in interceptions with 11, giving New England fans a legitimate reason to be concerned. Regardless of the situation around him, the Patriots have no chance if their quarterback can't turn it around. 3. The great outdoors: It's no secret that Jared Goff has trouble playing football when there is no roof above him. He is 1-2 in outdoor games this season, most recently defeating the Dolphins . However, Detroit's offense struggled to score points in Miami, resurfacing the questions about Goff's struggles when dealing with the elements. In fairness to Goff, he had a stellar game against the Bills earlier this season, though that did come with more ideal weather conditions. Unfortunately for the Lions, they are back outside this week in Germany and the forecast isn't as comfortable, with calls for temperatures in the 40s and 50s. Lions vs Patriots odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Lions (-1.5) Moneyline: Lions -120; Patriots +100 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Lions vs Patriots USA TODAY expert picks Adam Kaufman: Lions 30, Patriots 23 I'm more worried about who's blocking for Drake Maye than what time his alarm goes off. Will Campbell and Ben Brown both hurt their knees against Green Bay, A.J. Brown has missed two straight, and the backfield has its own injury questions with Corey Kiner in line for RB1 reps. Maye can still make enough plays to keep this interesting, especially if he gets some help back. But the Lions can put the Patriots in a bind with Jahmyr Gibbs on the ground and Jared Goff off play-action. It's hard not to trust the Lions to finish more drives after what we just watched in Foxborough. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Lions 30, Patriots 28 New England heads to Munich trying to leave its various problems stateside. Drake Maye could be in for a bounce-back performance if he can show more restraint with unforced errors. And it seems unfathomable that Christian Gonzalez could have two weeks of the kind of nightmare outing he was responsible for against the Packers . Still, Detroit's pass rush could create problems for Maye, and New England could have difficulty preventing this from turning into a shootout. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Lions 27, Patriots 21 Trusting Jared Goff to win a game without the luxury of climate control is not for the faint of heart, but the Lions are simply better at this stage. Detroit's offense, if it gets going, is something the New England can't keep up with – especially with the amount of injuries the team is dealing with. That will be the difference in Germany and Patriots fans will be left wondering if they're watching a repeat of the beatdown the Packers just gave them in Week 9. away.headline: AJ Brown injury update as Patriots WR eyes international game return
away.blurb: A.J. Brown returned to practice for the first time in two weeks on Wednesday, Nov. 11 and has received an injury designation of "questionable" for Week 10. The designation is an indication that Brown could play in the game despite only practicing in a limited capacity all week. In Week 1, the former Eagle suffered a high ankle sprain and missed four games. Brown returned for two more games despite limited participation in practice. In Week 8, a knee injury was added to his status on New England's injury report, and he missed five more practices and two more games before his Nov. 11 return. Brown has now practiced three straight days – albeit in a limited capacity – and traveled with the Patriots to Munich. Brown is questionable to play in the Patriots' Week 10 game against the Lions . This week is the first that Brown has a status other than "out" since Week 7. The star receiver has missed New England's last two games while dealing with injuries to his ankle and knee. The Patriots' official website reported that Brown traveled to Germany with the team ahead of their matchup with the Lions in Munich. According to the team's injury report, he was a limited participant with ankle and knee injuries in all three days of practice leading up to Sunday's game on Nov. 15. New England also has one of its top other three receivers out on injured reserve: Romeo Doubs with a shoulder. This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: A.J. These newcomers join a team that already holds a three-game lead in its division. They will also line up on the other side of the ball from an offense that is cooking with gas. The fourth-highest-scoring unit in the NFL has flat-out demolished half of its opponents. Trevor Lawrence , somehow, is still somewhat flying under the radar — probably because his offense keeps building such large leads that he does not need to rack up passing numbers in the second halves of these blowouts. Parker Washington has turned into a star, and Bhayshul Tuten emerged as a bona fide No. 1 running back. All of the pieces are in place. Just when it seemed like the Patriots were starting to put everything back together, they hit another rough patch. Just like they did to open the season, they have lost two of their last three games. The only win in that stretch was a five-point squeaker against the lowly Miami Dolphins . The road ahead does not get a whole lot easier with five likely playoff teams on the schedule over the next eight weeks. It is going to be a battle to return to the postseason after last year's run to the Super Bowl. Don't look now, but the Houston Texans are not out of it yet. The AFC South will remain out of reach so long as the Jaguars do not shockingly collapse, so it is Wild Card or bust for a squad that started the year at 0-4. At just 1.5 games back, the Texans are right in the mix. Since that winless first month of the season, the Texans have won three of four and took two of those games in blowout fashion. They just put up a season-high 44 points on the bottom-dwelling Los Angeles Chargers in a game that emphasized how far C.J. Stroud has come as a quarterback. He continues to play the best football of his career and is not even remotely the reason why the Texans are still two games under .500. Tank Dell's return to the wide receiver group and Marvin Harrison Jr.'s addition about a month ago also gave him a deep stable of pass-catchers to target, and he is cashing in. Losses are rare in the NFC North. At least one team has to add one to their tally in Week 10, though. The Packers are the only team with three losses, so every matchup means a little bit more to them as they try to work their way out of the shallow basement of the NFL's best division — one that could send all four teams to the postseason . They will have vengeance on their minds on Sunday as they seek to get payback for what the Minnesota Vikings did to them in a stunning second-half comeback in Week 1. home.headline: A big Munich test for Lions and Patriots as injuries loom for New England
home.blurb: Injuries are a top concern for New England. Before traveling Wednesday night, the Patriots ruled out LG Ben Brown (knee), CB Carlton Davis III (knee) and RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness). November 12, 2026 / 5:07 PM EST / AP Heading into international games, NFL coaches typically talk up the niceties of "growing the game" globally. The New England Patriots (5-4) have lost two of their past three games and have a slew of injury concerns, including running back Rhamondre Stevenson. The Detroit Lions, even with a 6-2 record and four straight victories, are trying to keep pace in the tight NFC North. Sunday's game in Munich is a big one for both teams. Lions coach Dan Campbell wasn't focused on the international implications. "Well, if I'm being honest, I just haven't thought that far into it. I'm like, 'We've got to get prepared,'" Campbell said. The Patriots were embarrassed at home by the Green Bay Packers last week, losing 45-27, with Drake Maye throwing three interceptions and the secondary struggling to contain the Packers' passing game. Campbell expects a much-improved New England team on Sunday. "You look at the totality of what this team is capable of, the firepower they have, and they're a good team. They're dangerous," he said. "And they're going to clean a lot of things up." The Lions slogged through a 19-9 win over the rebuilding Miami Dolphins last week, relying on four field goals from Jake Bates. It was also just one week after a neck injury to All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell. Detroit's bye week is in the rearview mirror, and after Munich, the team will host Tampa Bay and then Chicago on Thanksgiving Day. "It's a good thing to be tested during the season," Campbell said. "It really is. And to have to go through some of these tough stretches because that's what the playoffs are. That's what it is. And certainly if you got to go on the road. So, that's what this is. This is about us. This is the next obstacle we have. Told the team we're not going to clear it. Our objective is to go through it, and that's the mindset." Stevenson, the team's leading rusher with 399 yards on 102 carries, didn't practice Wednesday because of a knee injury. That could put second-year running back Corey Kiner in line for the bulk of the carries. "Corey has done a really nice job, but there are also some things that Corey has to be able to improve on," coach Mike Vrabel said, citing "recognition of the pressure and then the ability to block the pressure." The coach said "a lot of contending teams" are 5-4. "We've got to start putting ourselves in position to play meaningful games in January or in the middle of January," Vrabel said. "It's usually what happens in the National Football League; a bunch of teams get bunched up, and they go in different directions, and I know the direction that we're going to head in, and that's going to be the one that's forward, positive and winning." Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown likely had Week 10 circled on his calendar when the 2026 NFL schedule was released. Not only are the Lions facing the defending AFC-champion New England Patriots on Sunday, but the contest will be taking place in Munich, Germany. St. Brown's mother is originally from Germany and the four-time Pro Bowler holds dual American and German citizenship. The 27-year-old has missed just two games across his five-plus NFL seasons and has suited up in 58 straight contests. The last time that St. Brown was sidelined was in Week 5 of the 2023 campaign. St. Brown played a season-low 44 offensive snaps versus Miami , but this could be his only chance to play an NFL contest in Germany and Detroit needs a victory. Despite the Lions' 6-2 record and current four-game winning streak, they still trail the NFC North-leading Chicago Bears (7-2), are tied with the Minnesota Vikings (6-2) and just ahead of the Green Bay Packers (6-3). St. Brown told reporters (including Lions reporter Dave Birkett of the Detroit Free Press ) that he's ready to play on Sunday. "I just want to say thank you to everyone that’s here. All the fans, I can’t wait for the game," the two-time first team All-Pro said on Friday. "I’m so excited to be playing football in Germany with my teammates. It’s really honestly a dream come true. I haven’t even played the game yet and it feels amazing. The love, the support, the energy. I can’t wait to see the fans so, yeah, I’m ready."

The Falcons have lost four of their past five matchups but aren't technically out of it given the dire state of the NFC South. As a result, Kevin Stefanski's group is viewing this contest as a must-win if they want to stay in the playoff race. Despite Kansas City's impressive 6-2 record, Andy Reid and Co. have dealt with special teams struggles and offensive inconsistencies. Kenneth Walker III is a dynamic weapon in the backfield , but Bijan Robinson is on another level. He has three games in which he surpassed 100 yards this season and is averaging 5.2 yards per carry. Atlanta is unsurprisingly a significant underdog coming into this one, though it really depends on which version of the Falcons show up on Sunday. The drastic shifts in Atlanta's play have fans scratching their heads, largely due to the play of quarterback Michael Penix Jr. A week after taking home NFC Offensive Player of the Week honors in Week 7, he tossed a career-high four interceptions and failed to get his team a point. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jared Sapp · SB Nation Fri, November 13, 2026 at 9:30 PM UTC · 9 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs travel to face the Atlanta Falcons , our writers predicted the final score and result. Atlanta has been an unpredictable team both looking dominant in their trio of wins while struggling in most of their six losses. FanDuel Sportsbook currently lists the Chiefs as 3.5-point home favorites. The Falcons also have the misfortune of not coming off of a European game into their bye week. The Falcons lost 34-17 to the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid, Spain on Sunday. They also sent starting safety Jessie Bates to the Jacksonville Jaguars ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline. We also want to know your score prediction! Vote in the poll on The Feed and share your score prediction ! Jared Sapp ( @TrumanChief ) I do worry about the Falcons' pass rush, even if their defense's other two levels were underwhelming even before trading Bates. With the league's two best running backs facing off, I expect a run heavy day that should lead to a fast moving game. Look for the Chiefs' pass rush to build on their second half against Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix. This will be a game where Atlanta looks game for a couple of drives before the Chiefs overwhelm in route to a victory. The run game will lead to limited possessions for both sides to keep the scoring from getting out of hand. Chiefs 27, Falcons 17 Caleb James ( @CJScoobs ) The Chiefs and Falcons are on opposite ends of the competitive spectrum in the NFL, and this week's game should show that. The Falcons traded away veteran safety Jessie Bates to the contending Jacksonville Jaguars, while the Chiefs traded for wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts. Despite a talented core of offensive playmakers, including Bijan Robinson and Drake London, the Falcons are only 3-6, largely because their defense allows over 340 yards per game. The Falcons are -8 in the turnover-takeaway category, 30th in the NFL, while the Chiefs are tied for 9th at +4. If they can force turnovers, they will be in good shape to win the game. I don't think Downs will play more than 20 snaps this week, but I would expect the Chiefs to design a few routes for him to get his feet wet in the offense. Chiefs 27, Falcons 13 Mark Gunnels ( @MarkAGunnels ) I've got the Chiefs winning this one. Josh Downs makes his debut, and I like Mahomes having another guy who can get open underneath, especially now that Atlanta traded away Jessie Bates. The Falcons also traded their starting center, Ryan Neuzil, so I expect Chris Jones to make life real uncomfortable up the middle. Chiefs 27, Falcons 20 Maurice Elston ( @MrMauriceElston ) What impressed me most about the Chiefs' 35–12 win over the Jets was how they finished. Kansas City has a habit of letting teams it should beat hang around, and the Jets were within two points at halftime. The Chiefs outscored them 21–0 from there. Kenneth Walker III looked like the player we saw during the 5–0 start, finishing with 143 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns. To keep Walker rolling, the Chiefs need their receivers to win against man coverage. Seattle and Denver showed what happens when defenses can load the box and trust their corners to hold up one-on-one: the run slows down, and play-action loses its bite. If the receivers make Atlanta pay for that approach, Walker will have more room to run and Patrick Mahomes can get back to attacking off play-action. Against Atlanta, the key is slowing down Bijan Robinson. That's the operative phrase: slow him down. He's coming off 100 rushing yards and another 47 through the air, so Kansas City has to account for him even when he doesn't get the handoff. Drake London demands attention, and Kyle Pitts can still cause problems for the Chiefs' linebackers and safeties even in a quiet season. But if Kansas City's run defense keeps Robinson from taking over, Sack Nation can build on its five-sack performance by moving Michael Penix Jr. off his spot and forcing him past his first read. I like the Chiefs' chances when Atlanta has to win that way. Matt Stagner ( @stagdsp ) Your Kansas City Chiefs head to Atlanta as big favorites against the 2-6 Falcons. Yes, they've lost 4 of their last 5, but this is a dangerous opponent. They've got the league's best RB and a streaky young QB– it's an offense that can get out to an early lead and make things uncomfortable. But, as always, this game will come down to how the Chiefs execute. From the pass protection to the receivers and the short-yardage offense, this team has questions, but they're more than capable. Ideally, they start strong with Walker and Johnson– if the run game gets going, the Chiefs are hard to beat. Chiefs 33, Falcons 21 Dakota Watson ( @D_Watson56 ) The Chiefs enter this game after righting some of their wrongs last week against the Jets, although still with major question marks for a team intent on making a Super Bowl run. The Falcons, meanwhile, are on a two game losing skid after their upset win over the previously unbeaten San Francisco 49ers. I never quite know what to make of the Falcons. They're a team with some of the best offensive weapons in the entire NFL, yet they can't ever seem to put it all together. Since Jonathan Taylor in week 2, Bijan Robinson will be the best running back the Chiefs have faced all season. The Chiefs have been great defending the run in 2026, and I think they will be able to contain Robinson, but he will still get his yards. Defensively, the Chiefs should also be able to continue the positive momentum they established last week in pressuring the quarterback and leading to mistakes by the Falcons' offense. I'm excited to see what the Chiefs' offense has in store for new wide receiver Josh Downs. I'm keeping my expectations in check, however, as it always seems like the Chiefs onboard their wide receivers slowly. I expect Downs to play 35-50% of the team's snaps, but they will still be able to generate enough offense to take home the win. Rocky Magana ( @RockyMagana ) The Atlanta Falcons only show up for primetime games; they are garbage during noon kickoffs. Despite having multiple weapons on offense, namely running back Bijan Robinson and wide receiver Drake London, they can never seem to put it all together in the daytime. On the other hand, the Chiefs are coming off one of their best performances of the season, when the pass rush finally woke up and bullied a terrible team in the New York Jets. At the end of the day, I would expect the Chiefs offense to continue rolling while they ramp up new acquisition wide receiver Josh Downs. Chiefs 31, Atlanta 17 Nate Christensen Atlanta has been a surprisingly competitive team since quarterback Michael Penix Jr. came back. The Falcons have one of the dynamic duos of weapons in running back Bijan Robinson and Drake London. That alongside a decent offensive line has given the Falcons a shot to win any game. Their defense has been surprisingly competent, but after trading Jessie Bates, that will probably fall off. I expect Atlanta to have some nice drives against the Chiefs, but the game will play out similarly to the Jets game. At some point, the Chiefs pressure will get to a pocket-bound Penix and Atlanta won't be able to catch up offensively. Chiefs pull away in the second half. Chiefs 28, Falcons 17 Ron Kopp Jr. ( @RonOnChiefs ) If the Falcons hadn't traded away two starters this week, this would feel much more like a spot where the Chiefs could slip up. Still, noon kickoffs have seemed to come with slow starts for Kansas City this year, and this Falcons team still has a reason to fight to stay tied for first place in the NFC South. However, Atlanta has had more letdowns than triumphs this year, including a couple of weeks ago when the Tampa Bay Buccaneers ran for 342 yards as a team and didn't need a pass to win. This game should be a comfortable win for Kansas City because of its offense, leaning on the ground game once again to stay in rhtyhm and open up the middle of the field for passes. 2026 Standings Nate Chrstensen Maurice Elston Dakota Watson All nine panelists predicted the Chiefs to win by more than ten points. Ron (38-20) and Matt (28-13) had the most accurate Week 9 predictions with only 16 total points of error. Our readers were less optimistic about how Kansas City would perform. Only 50.6% of our readers anticipated a comfortable Chiefs victory, while 37.2% expected Mahomes and Company to narrowly come out on top. 12.2% of respondents expected the Jets to win. *To calculate a prediction's points of error, the differences between the prediction and the actual score in point spread, home team score, and away team score are added together. For example, a prediction calls for a 17-10 Chiefs win. They end up winning 16-10, so there were two points of error: the point spread was off by one point, the Kansas City score missed by one point, and the opponent's score was predicted correctly. But if the Chiefs lose the game 17-10, there were 28 points of error in the prediction: the point spread was off by 14 (the difference between +7 and -7), and both scores were off by 7.

picks.headline: Chiefs-Falcons betting line & prediction: Will Josh Downs make instant impact?
picks.blurb: Read our AI Policy. The Chiefs acquired receiver Josh Downs, who is expected to debut Sunday in Atlanta. Patrick Mahomes practiced fully Wednesday after an elbow injury scare vs. Jets. The betting line lists Kansas City as a 3.5-point favorite over Atlanta. The Kansas City Chiefs stopped a two-game losing streak Sunday with their 35-12 win over the New York Jets to improve to 6-2. Earlier Sunday, the Atlanta Falcons lost their second straight game, falling 34-17 to the Cincinnati Bengals at Santiago Bernabéu Stadium in Madrid, Spain. The loss dropped Atlanta to 3-6. How to watch Chiefs at Falcons Kickoff: Noon Central Where: Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta TV: CBS (Channel 5 in Kansas City) Radio: KFNZ (96.5 FM in Kansas City, KNSS 98.7 FM in Wichita) Betting line: Chiefs -3.5 Behind the KC-ATL matchup The Chiefs and Falcons look a little different than they did last week, before the NFL’s trade deadline. Kansas City made the highly anticipated move Tuesday to acquire wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts . Meanwhile, Atlanta began the week by agreeing to trade three-time second-team All-Pro safety Jessie Bates to the Jacksonville Jaguars before sending starting center Ryan Neuzil to the Baltimore Ravens. Downs is expected to make his Chiefs debut Sunday in Atlanta. He recorded 33 catches for 354 yards and a touchdown for the Colts this season. Downs’ stat line included seven catches for 72 yards against Kansas City in Week 2. “I had to watch him live. Yeah, which wasn’t good,” Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Wednesday, drawing laughter from reporters. To earn extended playing time Sunday, Downs will have to demonstrate that he can handle Reid’s complex playbook. Kansas City kept that in mind while shopping for receivers. “That’s what we felt about Josh — that he has that ability,” Reid said. “And now it’s just a matter of him spending the time to knock it out. But he’s a pretty alert kid.” How Downs fits alongside Travis Kelce, Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy will be worth watching, but the good news for the Chiefs is that his debut should come with Patrick Mahomes under center. Mahomes suffered an injury scare late in the second quarter against the Jets. Mahomes hurt his elbow but remained in the game, and medical test results were encouraging. He was listed as a full participant in Wednesday’s practice. In an encouraging development, Worthy (hamstring) also participated fully. “I feel like I’m in a great spot,” Mahomes said. “Now it’s just about pain and pain management and stuff like that, which I’ll try to do whatever I can to be in the best place possible.” While much of the focus will be on Downs’ Chiefs debut and how Mahomes attacks a Falcons secondary playing its first game without Bates, the path to victory is likely to look familiar. Running back Kenneth Walker presents a favorable matchup against an Atlanta defense allowing 4.4 yards per carry. After two less productive games by his lofty standards, Walker rushed 18 times for 102 yards against the Jets , adding four receptions for 41 yards and three total touchdowns. Following his breakout performance in Denver, rookie Emmett Johnson rushed for 34 yards and a touchdown on six carries against New York. Asked about the Falcons’ defense, Reid highlighted edge rusher James Pearce, who returned last week for 15 snaps after serving an eight-game suspension to begin the season. The former first-round pick registered 10.5 sacks as a rookie in 2025. Pearce (back) missed practice Wednesday, so his status is worth monitoring. “(The Falcons are) fast — and even faster when they’re on their turf,” Reid said. “So they’re very athletic. They’ve got some young linebackers that are flying around. They’ve got that front, and they rotate those guys.” With right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) out of practice Wednesday, Josh Ezeudu could be in line to make his second start of the season. Pearce can line up on either side of the line, and he will be a challenge for both Ezeudu and Chiefs left tackle Kahlil Benson. The Falcons feature 11 players with at least one sack, including defensive end Za’Darius Smith (4.5), defensive end Cameron Thomas (2) and defensive tackle LaCale London (2) — all with at least two sacks on the season. On offense, the Falcons’ biggest threat is running back Bijan Robinson, the only player in the league with more rushing yards (880) than Walker (872), though with one additional game. “He’s electricity in a bottle,” Chiefs linebacker Nick Bolton said of Robinson. “That’s what I say. (He’s) able to change direction, get upfield, cutbacks. We see all the time everybody’s at the point of attack because he can cut it back and put pressure on the back-side corner on the outside zone to the opposite side. So he’s electricity in a bottle, like I said, and it’ll take all hands on deck.” Much like Kansas City, Atlanta wants its running game to create opportunities through the air. Robinson’s presence helps open things up for quarterback Michael Penix Jr. and wide receiver Drake London, who leads the Falcons with 692 receiving yards but only one touchdown. The Chiefs listed cornerback Mansoor Delane (shoulder) as a full participant Wednesday, and his return after a two-game absence would help Kansas City match up against London. Kansas City’s defensive front will look to build on its momentum after sacking Jets quarterback Geno Smith five times last Sunday. Defensive end George Karlaftis and defensive tackle Chris Jones recorded two sacks apiece. According to NFL NextGen Stats, Penix posts a league-worst 34% completion percentage when under pressure. Jones should have an advantage over center Corey Levin, who is expected to make his first start of the season after replacing Neuzil. A sixth-round pick in 2017, Levin has spent most of his career in a reserve role. Despite kicker Harrison Butker’s recent struggles, Reid announced Wednesday that he would stick with him for now, with Justin Tucker waiting on the practice squad. Perhaps a homecoming for Butker, an Atlanta native, sparks the turnaround he’s been seeking. Chiefs-Falcons game prediction As evidenced by their respective deadline moves, the Chiefs are all in on 2026, as the Falcons look toward the future. Kansas City draws energy from Downs’ debut, Delane helps neutralize London and the pass rush builds on last week’s solid outing. Since Week 4, he ranks second in the league in adjusted EPA per play and sixth in completion percentage over expected. Last week against the Chargers, he proved that he didn't need to rely solely on throwing the ball to Nico Collins either, spreading his targets across the entire Texans' receiving corps. Meanwhile, the Browns are seemingly making the decision to go back to Deshaun Watson at quarterback after Shedeur Sanders put up a strong performance in their Week 9 overtime loss to the Saints. To me, that brings down their rating ahead of this week. I'll lay the points with the Texans on the road. Pick: Texans -4 (-109) via Caesars I completely agree with MacMillan in this game. Houston is much better than it showed early in the season, and the Texans do appear to be turning a corner as of late. The Browns have made a few questionable decisions, and I think they’ve already played their best football of the season. The division may be out of reach as the Jaguars lead the Texans by three games in the AFC South but Houston is back in the race for a Wild Card spot. Cleveland takes the field after dropping their last two games which has dropped them out of first in the AFC North and 1.5 games behind the Steelers and the Bengals. Houston is coming off its most explosive performance of the season, a 44-22 road rout of the winless Los Angeles Chargers. C.J. Stroud played through an illness and completed 21 of 35 passes for 384 yards, five touchdowns and one interception. He connected with four different players for scores, including 63-yard touchdowns to Tank Dell and Kayshon Boutte , with Boutte finishing with 125 receiving yards and two touchdowns. The Texans led 24-9 at halftime, stretched the advantage to 38-9 early in the fourth quarter and defensively overwhelmed Justin Herbert , sacking him eight times. home.blurb: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans made it known that Montgomery's status has improved from last week ––when he was ruled out with a groin injury on Wednesday––but said he would continue to be evaluated throughout the week. It remains to be seen if he ends up playing once the weekend rolls around. Azeez Al-Shaair might be a name to keep an eye on, as he was a DNP with seemingly the same groin injury that's restricted his availability in practice as of late . However, given that he also had a personal designation, there's a better chance that he'll be good to go for either Thursday or Friday's session. Tight end Brevin Jordan also wound up as a DNP in practice with a finger/foot issue. If he's unable to go against the Browns, Houston has four other tight ends on the roster to turn to instead, including second-round rookie Marlin Klein, who was active on the gameday against the LA Chargers for the first time since Week 4. The Texans' final status for everyone on the roster will become clearer after Friday's practice. But until then, keep a close watch on those four who didn't practice, while also not losing sight of anyone who was limited for Wednesday’s action. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Imagn Images Week 10 in the NFL is here, and it's the first week where all the players who were dealt at the trade deadline will make their debuts with their new teams. Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings , the Jacksonville Jaguars traded for three new defensive players, including Jordan Davis , and the Kansas City Chiefs gave Patrick Mahomes a new wideout in Josh Downs . Which one of these additions will be most beneficial for a Super Bowl run? This Sunday, the New England Patriots and Detroit Lions will battle in Germany, the Vikings and Green Bay Packers play an important divisional matchup and the Cincinnati Bengals look to steal the AFC North lead from the Pittsburgh Steelers . Which teams should you pick in Week 10, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 11 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research New England Patriots vs. Detroit Lions (-2.5) (Munich) Dajani (Lions -2.5): It's going to take me some time to get over watching the Patriots have 45 points dropped on their face by the Packers. Drake Maye threw three interceptions, and the team could now be down its top two running backs. Rhamondre Stevenson is reportedly dealing with a knee injury, while TreVeyon Henderson experienced an " unusual medical emergency ." That leaves the Patriots with Corey Kiner and Lan Larison at running back. When it comes to the Lions, the question has never been about Jared Goff 's offense but about Kelvin Sheppard 's defense. No one is talking about it, but this unit has been better in recent weeks. In fact, over this four-game win streak, they rank second in points allowed per game (15.5) and yards allowed per game (286.3). Give me the Lions. … Prediction: Lions 28, Patriots 20 Dubin (Lions -2.5): The Patriots' rapidly thinning skill-position corps gives me some doubt that they can compete with the Lions offensively. Especially after New England's secondary was just lit up by the Packers, I can see Detroit having some passing game success here, bouncing back from a slow last two weeks through the air. And then Jahmyr Gibbs is always liable to go off. Drake Maye is capable of single-handedly carrying an offense against a bad defense, but as Dajani said, Detroit's defense has been playing better as of late. … Prediction: Lions 30, Patriots 21 Kansas City Chiefs (-3.5) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Chiefs -3.5): I initially wanted to take the points here with the Atlanta Falcons , but they just got home from Madrid and sent safety Jessie Bates III to the Jaguars at the trade deadline. The Falcons were dominated by the Bengals abroad, 34-17, meaning they have lost back-to-back games by at least 16 points. The Falcons' run defense will have to be ready for Kenneth Walker III , but I think the key to not getting caught by the hook could be Josh Downs, who the Chiefs acquired this week at the trade deadline. He's not some downfield perimeter threat, but is a slot weapon that could spark Patrick Mahomes' passing game. … Prediction: Chiefs 26, Falcons 21 Dubin (Chiefs -3.5): Atlanta has been getting clobbered on the ground lately (123 or more rushing yards allowed in four of the last five games and 200 or more twice) and is about to run into the Kenneth Walker train. The Chiefs finally added someone who can beat man coverage in Josh Downs, and while it might take him a few weeks to get fully up to speed, he should help them immediately in situational football. Plus, the Chiefs' defense has been really good against both the run and the pass. This line seems several points too low. … Prediction: Chiefs 27, Falcons 16 Minnesota Vikings at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Dajani (Vikings +3.5): I don't know how much time Kirk Cousins is going to need to get acclimated to his (somewhat) new situation in Minnesota, but I bet this organization and this defense are JUICED to add him to the fold. Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz simply weren't cutting it, and Cousins has actually been playing some good ball out in Vegas. His 20 passing touchdowns rank second in the NFL, and his 260.0 passing yards per game rank eighth. Cousins also has chemistry with Justin Jefferson , whose 98.9 receiving yards per game when catching passes from Cousins are the most by a QB-WR duo all-time. This Packers passing attack has been lethal with Jordan Love playing MVP football and Christian Watson and Matthew Golden looking like prime Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle , but give me the Vikings to keep it close. … Prediction: Packers 20, Vikings 17 Dubin (Vikings +3.5): In-division rematches are typically lower scoring than the first matchup, so like Dajani, I see a fairly low-scoring game here despite the fact that the Packers' offense has been a fireworks show and the Vikings just upgraded their quarterback situation. These two defenses are playing extraordinarily well right now, and I think they'll be able to get a handle on what each offense is doing. It's official: Poch to Man United Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Packers vs. Vikings Odds: Opening line for Week 10 matchup (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Justis Mosqueda · SB Nation Mon, November 9, 2026 at 6:40 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Green Bay Packers (6-3) are set to be three-point favorites over the Minnesota Vikings (6-1) in Week 10, according to FanDuel's numbers . That number comes with a little juice at -120, and the Packers are -178 favorites, which comes with an implied probability of 64 percent. If you had said this a few weeks ago, when the Packers' offensive line was drowning, no one would have bought it. Now, after Green Bay finally had a 100-yard rushing performance and beat down on the New England Patriots in all three phases of the game, it looks like the Packers have a real opportunity to make a push for the postseason. The Vikings have played two fewer games than the Packers because: 1) they've already had their bye week and 2) they're playing on Monday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills. After that game, they'll have a short(er) week and have to travel on the road to Lambeau Field. Their starting quarterback, Kyler Murray, is currently dealing with a hamstring injury and will not play against the Bills. We'll have to see if it heals up by the time they kick off against the Packers, or if it'll be Carson Wentz — their current replacement starter — under center. The only other quarterback in Minnesota is Max Brosmer (53-man roster). Below is the current playoff picture in the NFC: San Francisco 49ers: 7-1 (NFC West) Minnesota Vikings: 6-1 (NFC North) New York Giants: 5-2-1 (NFC East) Carolina Panthers: 3-5 (NFC South) Chicago Bears: 7-2 Detroit Lions: 6-2 Green Bay Packers: 6-3 Seattle Seahawks: 5-4 Los Angeles Rams: 5-4 Dallas Cowboys: 4-5 New Orleans Saints: 3-5 Tampa Bay Buccaneers: 3-6 Atlanta Falcons: 3-6 Arizona Cardinals: 3-6 Washington Commanders: 2-5-1 Philadelphia Eagles: 2-7 The Packers are holding onto the seventh seed right now, where they've been for weeks, but the NFC North keeps winning — as do the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams, the teams trying to hunt them down from behind. The NFC is so wonky, with the "good" teams being in the North and West, not the South and East, that the 3-6 Tampa Bay Buccaneers currently have about as good a chance of making the playoffs (by winning the NFC South) as do the Los Angeles Rams (a .500 team that is essentially locked into a playoff spot or nothing in 2026), per The Athletic's playoff simulator . In short, there are seven North and West teams fighting for five playoff spots in the NFC, and then there's whatever the hell is happening in the East and South. Do not be surprised at all if a sub-.500 NFC South team ends up hosting a 12-5 (or better record) NFC North team in the wild card round this year.

While none of the four analysts gave score predictions, they all predict the Minnesota Vikings will improve to 7-2 with a statement win at Lambeau Field. Louis Riddick, Andrew Hawkins, Will Compton, and Taylor Lewan all chose the Vikings over the Packers in Sunday's NFC North showdown. It's important to remember what the Vikings did to GB in Week 1, though that game was played in Minnesota. Packers fans will go back to the officials in that one, but ultimately, there's no excuse for giving up 29 unanswered points. It feels like those days are behind the Packers, but with head coach Matt LaFleur at the helm, anything can happen on Sunday, Nov. 15. Micah Parsons is still two weeks out from returning, but this Packers defense has been unbelievable the past few weeks. There were a few breakdowns in coverage against the New England Patriots, but it didn't matter as Jordan Love played out of his mind . Love leads the league in passing, and one could argue he now has the most dynamic receiving duo in the NFL. On the other side, Justin Jefferson is stuck doing absolutely nothing in this Vikings offense. He has just 31 receptions for 393 yards this season. For reference, Love threw for 387 yards in Week 1. Tucker Kraft, who's coming off a torn ACL, is only 42 yards shy of Jefferson's total this season. Both Matthew Golden (14.8) and Christian Watson (17.9) are well ahead of Jefferson's 12.7 yards per reception, and it's really not even close. Now with Kirk Cousins back, it should give Jefferson an opportunity to emerge as a dominant WR1 once again. Once Carson Wentz came into the game in Week 1, Jefferson exploded with his best game of the year. He finished with eight receptions on nine targets for 92 yards with a pair of touchdowns. Defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon has had plenty of time to settle into his new role, so now just over two months later, it'll be interesting to see what adjustments he makes. No one is denying the fact that the Vikings' defense is legit, but Love has blossomed into a true MVP candidate this season, and with what he did against Minnesota in Week 1, it's crazy to think the entire Get Up crew predicted the Packers would fall to 6-4.

away.headline: Senior NFL insider has high hopes for Vikings following Kirk Cousins trade
away.blurb: He also pointed out how Cousins just immediately took charge from day one of returning to his former team. Related Articles NFL Insider Explains Ravens’ Lamar Jackson Return Window Let us be frank: The moment the world heard that Kirk Cousins would be returning to the Minnesota Vikings mere hours before Tuesday’s trade deadline, there was a sigh of relief from fans that was so loud, it broke the sound barrier. So, naturally, insiders and professionals alike are weighing in about how the rest of the Vikings season can look with Cousins back in the driver’s seat, including NFL senior insider Ian Rapoport. “I feel like if they can just play like, average offense, and they should be better than that, but if they can play average offense, this becomes one of the best teams in the NFL because their defense is so good,” Rapoport said on “The Pat McAfee Show” on Friday when asked how big Cousins’ first game back against the Green Bay Packers will be. “And that’s what I kind of liked about this move for the Vikings is they clearly feel like because their defense is so good, we have an opportunity, we have to seize it. Whatever it costs, like, whatever happens, it’s like get a viable quarterback and just get this thing rolling. You know, they now get a boost for the second half of the year. “I think Cousins is going to hit the ground running. It’s an incredible opportunity to bring back someone who has been in the system, who they loved, who is playing really good football at 38-years-old like, this is an excellent situation for the Minnesota Vikings.” What makes a huge difference is Minnesota is where Cousins wants to be and where his teammates and coaches want him to be. Especially receiver Justin Jefferson, who said that welcoming Cousins back was a “joy.” “He just understands the game,” Jefferson said, ESPN reported . “He’s a guy that studies the game a lot. He understands how the defenses play, especially covering me. And he understands, the plays that we have called that are kind of my plays and he understands the timing and the windows to throws those type of plays, but he also doesn’t force those type of plays to me and he just lets the game come to me.” “He’s being vocal,” Jefferson continued. “Just making sure that everybody hears the plays that he’s talking about and the notes that he has for certain routes, certain plays. And he’s just making sure that everybody’s on the same page. So it’s definitely cool to hear that type of leadership and command. If you know Kirk, that’s pretty normal from him. away.headline: Packers must corral Vikings return man Myles Price
away.blurb: Under the guidance of new coordinator Cam Achord, the Packers’ special teams have been — with some exceptions — generally pretty solid. Pre-injury, Skyy Moore bolstered the Packers’ return game, but the Packers’ special teams have really shined in coverage. As of this week, the Packers’ have allowed the fourth-lowest average per return on punt returns and the 10th lowest figure on special teams. (This, incidentally, aligns with the special teams stuff the Packers have historically cared about the most and done the best, but it’s still good to see them doing a good job there.) But as good as the Packers are in punt and kick coverage, the Vikings are even better at punt and kick returns. Minnesota currently ranks first in punt return average (17.5 yards per return) and second in kickoff return average (29.9 per return). It’s true the Vikings have logged a very long punt return (86 yards) and a pretty long kickoff return (68 yards), but even if you removed those long returns, the Vikings’ averages would only drop them to the fifth- and third-best spots in the league on punt and kickoff return, respectively. And it’s all thanks to return man Myles Price. Undrafted out of Indiana in 2025, the 5-foot-9, 183-pound Price was a special teams only player for the Vikings last season. He averaged a respectable 9.9 yards per return on 30 punt returns and 25.9 yards per return on 60 kickoff returns, but capped out at a long of 43 yards on his punt duties and 61 yards on kickoff returns. Certainly not bad numbers, but not eye popping. That’s changed in 2026. The pocket-sized Price leads the NFL in punt return yardage, boasts the longest punt return in the league, and is the only player in the NFL to score on a punt return this season. He’s also the only player who’s returned either a punt or a kick for the Vikings this year, meaning their impressive league-wide rankings are entirely the work of their micro machine return man. The Vikings’ defense is incredible. Their offense should be more capable with a new quarterback under center. But their special teams also present a very interesting challenge for the Packers. Everybody knows the Packers will have their hands full with Brian Flores, and Kirk Cousins may be enough to bolster their offense to at least some level of respectability. But if the Packers don’t take care of business on special teams, the Vikings could end up tilting the balance in that phase of the game. And in what’s expected to be a close game, any little bit could make a difference. Fortunately, special teams have never been a game-altering problem for the Packers in the past, right? Right?
