The 6-2 Jaguars are set to travel to Nissan Stadium to face the Tennessee Titans in Week 10, their first game since making blockbuster trades for Jessie Bates and Jordan Davis, along with adding Davon Godchaux for a sixth-round pick. For a Jaguars team that has their eyes set on an AFC South title and a top seed in the playoffs, they are treating the Titans with the same seriousness that they treated the Indianapolis Colts and Baltimore Ravens over the last two weeks. So, how do we see the Jaguars' Week 10 battle with the Titans playing out? We break it down below. Jessie Bates Records An Interception While it certainly remains to be seen if the Jaguars will actually play any of their new defensive pieces against the Titans, I believe they will. Jakobi Meyers and Greg Newsome each played in their first games with the franchise last season after joining the team during that same week, and I think that means we see the trio make their Jaguars debuts. In the process, I think we see Bates create his first Jaguars takeaway right off the bat. Cam Ward is far from the most turnover-prone quarterback the Jaguars have played this season; that distinction goes to Daniel Jones. But he is right near the league average in interception rate, and he has made some egregious decisions with the ball over his last two seasons as a starter. This feels like the perfect week for Anthony Campanile to cook some pressure looks up to confuse Ward, and Bates is a natural playmaker. I think we see his impact right away. Parker Washington Catches 2 TDs The Titans' defense has been ... not very good against slot receivers this season. The Titans rank in the bottom-5 in the NFL against slot targets in each of the following categories: yards per play allowed, yards after the catch allowed, yards after the catch over expectation, and average seperation. The Titans have simply been a mess in the slot, even moving long-time outside cornerback Alontae Taylor to the slot despite signing him in March to play on the outside. As a result, I think this is a Parker Washington week. He is the clear No. 1 receiver in the offense, and I think he shakes off some inconsistent moments we have seen as of late and has a huge game against the Titans. Washington is due for a big performance, and I think we see it this Sunday against the Titans. Cam Ward Throws For Fewer Than 150 Yards There have been 275 quarterback performances this season. In just 39 of those performances, we have seen quarterbacks throw for fewer than 150 yards. Cam Ward makes up two of those games, a number that is trumped only by Bo Nix and Malis Willis which is, well, not great company to be in as far as productive gunslingers go. Ward has been more productive and explosive as of late and is coming off one of the best games of his career, but I predict the Jaguars limit Ward to under 150. Ward threw for just 141 yards against the Jaguars in Week 13 a year ago, and the Jaguars limited Daniel Jones and Joe Fagnano to a combined 189 yards over the last eight quarters. The Jaguars' pass defense is clicking, largely due to the work of defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile, and I believe we see it continue this week. Jaguars Limit Tony Pollard to Under 4.0 YPC Titans running back Tony Pollard has been on a tear over the last few weeks. Pollard, who has rushed for 246 yards and five touchdowns over the last two games, broke out of a mid-season skid and has been able to average over 4.0 yards per carry in every single game but two this season. While Pollard has been one of the NFL's more impressive runners over the last few weeks, I expect the Jaguars to be ready to bottle him up on Sunday. Again, I think the Jaguars will play Davis and Godchaux on Sunday. But even if they don't, I do not think the Titans have the offense to keep the Jaguars off-balance enough to run the ball on them. Teams can only run the ball on the Jaguars when the Jaguars are threatened by the early-down pass, and I do not see the Titans having much success there. Walker Little Pitches Another Shutout The Jaguars have seen Walker Little play really, really well over the last few weeks since stepping into the lineup for an injured Anton Harrison. According to NextGenStats, Little has allowed pressure on just 6.4% of his pass blocks, the fifth lowest rate in the league among left tackles (minimum 100 pass blocks). On his 109 pass blocks, his 87.2% 1-on-1 matchup rate is the highest in the league among left tackles; his 6.3% 1-on-1 pressure rate allowed is the third lowest pressure rate allowed in the league. “The experience always helps. Confidence is a heck of a thing, and I think he's the one that said it in an interview that humility helped. Where obviously he became our swing tackle, and all that guy has done is just stay the course," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said on Wednesday. "Like, never got up, too down. He's just very steady. I really like Walker's play demeanor, the look in his eye recently and not taking everything so seriously. He's able to have fun with it. He's out there playing a game that he loves and competes with, but he's playing at a high level right now. He's got confidence, and you can tell.” Little will mostly draw Titans pass-rusher Jacob Martin, who has had a good year. But after strong showings against the Houston Texans' pass-rush duo in London a month ago and then a dominant outing against Trey Hendrickson last week , I think Little has the edge entering Week 10. He is playing some of the best football of his career right now, and I predict it leads to another shutout. Fans wouldn't be blamed for forgetting that we've got football this coming Sunday after days on end filled with rumors and breaking news at the end of every sentence. Not only do the Titans play in Week 10, but they're hosting AFC South-rivals. The Jacksonville Jaguars, one of the most active buyers at the trade deadline, are coming to Nashville to boast their new pickups. The last time Tennessee faced Jacksonville, the Titans lost 41-7 at the very end of the 2025 season. Cam Ward missed the majority of that game after exiting early with a shoulder injury, and his healthy showing tomorrow is the key to a potential Titans upset. Will: Cam Ward stays hot in Carnell Tate's return Ward nearly led Tennessee to a victory over the (now) 6-2 Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. The Titans falling short 36-43 in overtime was partly due to Ward taking a costly sack late in regulation, but the QB can't at all be blamed for losing a game he kept Tennessee in. With WR1 Carnell Tate trending toward a return, Ward should have all of his weapons in place to put up another promising game. The Titans even kept RB Tony Pollard at the deadline for Ward's own sake. Again, Jacksonville bulked up at the deadline - their defense specifically - but Tennessee leaving the offense untouched said loud and clear that this franchise believes in Ward. With a newly-gutted defense, the Titans will be relying on Ward to try and secure the win. Won't: Jaguars' overhauled defense clicks immediately Directly opposing Ward is that new-look Jags defense. In addition to adding All-Pro S Jessie Bates III, Jacksonville also acquired defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux. If Tennessee falls short (as is likely expected), it will be because the Jaguars' defense put a stopper in Ward and the offense's growth. That could be one reason among many, but it seems to be the most relevant by far regarding this specific matchup. Prediction: Titans lose, 34-23 At the end of the day on Sunday, I expect Jacksonville will overwhelm Tennessee. I don't believe it will be in blowout fashion, and this is primarily because of the stable flashes of progress Ward showed in Week 8. Perhaps the home field will help blunt the blow, as well as the team debuting their Music City jerseys. I love the jerseys. I like what we saw from Cam Ward in his most recent game. away.blurb: Jacksonville’s trade deadline splashes sitting out against Tennessee Those two additions round out a defensive unit that, when healthy, leaves Jacksonville with no real holes on paper as it chases a championship. A detail that’s easy to lose track of at the trade deadline is how bye weeks shake out for traded players. Because teams take their byes at different points on the calendar, a player can get robbed of his bye entirely if his old team hadn’t had one yet and his new team already did. On the flip side, some players luck into two. In the case of both Bates and Davis, neither had a bye this season until the Jaguars decided to hold them out against Tennessee. That gives them time to get up to speed mentally and to get some rest and recovery at the midpoint of the season before a push down the stretch, when it matters most for Jacksonville. home.headline: Titans announce unfortunate injury news for rookie WR Carnell Tate
home.blurb: Tennessee Titans rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate missed the first game of his NFL career in Week 8, ruled out with a shoulder injury. The Titans officially ruled Tate out for Sunday’s Week 10 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars. With Tate out again this weekend, Cam Ward and the Tennessee offense will continue to lean on Wan’Dale Robinson, Chimere Dike, Elic Ayomanor and Calvin Ridley as their WR options. Tate, the No. 4 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, had an extra week to recover over the Titans’ bye. However, he was unable to take the practice field for any action this week as he continues to deal with the lingering issue. “I was really optimistic going through the bye week. It’s just, the shoulder’s stuck on him a little bit,” head coach Robert Saleh said when speaking to reporters on Friday. “We’re hopeful for next week, but I’ll have a better answer for you guys come Wednesday.” After a relatively slow start to his NFL career, Tate exploded for 145 yards on nine catches in a Week 4 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens. The former Ohio State standout logged his first professional touchdown in a win over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 6. Through seven games in his first season with the Titans, Tate has 34 catches for 413 yards and one score. Sunday’s game against the Jaguars will kick off at 1 p.m. ET. They got close against the Cowboys, but the seventh loss this season marks doom. The Dolphins are coming to town, so this might be their best shot at win number three on the year. FanDuel Sportsbook favors the Colts to start with a 2.5-point spread advantage. The money line is -138 while the over/under sits at 43.5. The Colts had a rough Sunday. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Miami Dolphins (1-7) and Indianapolis Colts (2-7) meet Sunday at Lucas Oil Stadium in a matchup between two teams racing towards the top of the 2027 Draft. The Dolphins have lost two straight and sit in the cellar in the AFC East while the Colts have lost five in a row and have only the Titans between them and a spot in the basement in the AFC South. The headline as these teams take the field is that Miami’s starting signal-caller, Malik Willis , has been placed on the IR and as a result, rookie Kyle McCord will get the first start of his career. Indianapolis will continue with Daniel Jones , who has 1,722 passing yards and six touchdowns this season. Jones, however, has struggled to regain the form he had prior to tearing his Achilles late last season. Miami’s latest setback was a 19-9 home loss to the Detroit Lions, a game in which the Dolphins’ defense did enough to give the offense a chance but Miami never reached the end zone. Willis completed just 13 of 25 passes for 128 yards with an interception, while Ollie Gordon II led the Dolphins with 55 rushing yards and Caleb Douglas caught six passes for 70 yards. Miami finished with only 228 total yards, went 0-for-3 in the red zone and settled for three Zane Gonzalez field goals. Indianapolis’ last loss was considerably more painful. The Colts rallied from a 17-7 halftime deficit against Dallas, getting a 55-yard touchdown catch from Ashton Dulin and field goals of 59 and 50 yards from Spencer Shrader to take a 23-20 lead with 1:37 remaining. But Dak Prescott immediately hit Ryan Flournoy for 46 yards, and Javonte Williams scored from a yard out with 1:08 left to give Dallas a 27-23 victory. Jones finished 20-of-34 for 180 yards, a touchdown and an interception, while Jonathan Taylor managed only 46 yards on 13 carries and lost a costly fourth-quarter fumble. Dallas piled up 508 yards to Indianapolis’ 271, illustrating the biggest concern for a Colts’ team that is allowing 361.8 yards and 27.7 points per game. The central storyline, then, is which struggling offense can take advantage of an accommodating opponent. Miami is averaging only 15.8 points per game, 31st in the league, and will be asking McCord to make his debut on the road; Indianapolis averages 20.4 points but carries a -11 turnover differential, making ball security especially important for Jones and Taylor. Recent history favors the Colts. Indianapolis has won the last three meetings, including a 33-8 rout at Lucas Oil Stadium in Week 1 of the 2025 season, when Jones completed 22 of 29 passes for 272 yards and a touchdown and Taylor rushed for 71 yards. The broader history belongs to the Dolphins, who hold a 48-30 advantage across 78 regular-season and postseason meetings. away.headline: Dolphins Hit With Unfortunate Aaron Brewer News in Latest Injury Report
away.blurb: 'Who Let the Dogs Out'? The only other player who has now been hit with a DNP (did not participate) is rookie wide receiver Chris Bell. Bell is still dealing with a knee injury, which is connected to his torn ACL that he suffered at the end of his collegiate career in 2025. Bell has appeared on the injury report off and on since returning in Week 1 to play, and now he was downgraded from a limited participant on Wednesday to DNP on Thursday. Long snapper Tucker Addington (shoulder), cornerback Darrell Baker Jr. (knee ), edge Malik Herring (neck), tight end Will Kacmarek (quad/knee), and wide receiver Jared Wayne (quad) were all limited. Some good news in these listed players is that Kacmarek was upgraded to limited after missing Thursday's practice. Baker also remains limited, which could mean that he is not yet ready to play. The cornerback has made his return to practice after not playing in 2026 due to suffering a knee injury in training camp. There is still a chance that Baker could play, but the usual case is that players who remain limited likely need a week or so more to fully get back to being able to take the field. Wright has been dealing with a quad injury that led to him being ruled out in Week 9. Now, he is set to return against the Colts. Brewer has now missed his second straight practice, as he is currently in concussion protoco l. It is not unlikely that he will suit up against the Indianapolis Colts. The full injury report is as follows: Running back Kaytron Allen (quad), safety Michael Taaffe (wrist), safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin), and running back Jaylen Wright (quad) were all full participants yet again. Despite the semblance of a laundry list of injured players, the Dolphins look to be in decent shape. Losing Brewer will be a huge hit to the offense, but Andrew Meyer will be there to step in. Meyer spoke on Thursday about not only learning from "the best center in the league" but also stating that he has the confidence to step in for the Miami offensive line if that is what happens. The Dolphins are looking for their second win of the season, as they will face the struggling Colts. Indianapolis may not be a pushover opponent, but they also got rid of many players at the trade deadline, leaving this to be a potential "easier" matchup for Miami.

away.headline: Breaking Down the Good News/Bad News Regarding Dolphins WR Chris Bell
away.blurb: Head coach Jeff Hafley said that Bell likely would be listed as doubtful for the game at Lucas Oil Stadium because of a knee injury, but the good news here is that it's not related to the torn ACL that Bell sustained last November during his final season at Louisville. Instead, Bell was injured in practice Wednesday when he took a hit to the knee. He wound up being listed as limited for that day, didn't practice Thursday and Hafley he also wasn't going to practice Friday. The only other player that Hafley said would be out is wide receiver Jared Wayne, who sustained a quad injury in practice Thursday. His absence should mean a return to the lineup for veteran wide receiver Jalen Tolbert, who's had a pretty forgettable season after signing with the Dolphins as a free agent in the spring. Lastly, Hafley repeated what he had said before about rookie linebacker Trey Moore, who remains on IR with a pretty significant ankle injury he sustained in the preseason opener at Washington. Hafley said he was "hopeful" that Moore would be able to return at some point this season, though that time doesn't appear imminent and it's probably 50-50 that he'll be back at all in 2026. Breaking Down the Good News/Bad News Regarding Dolphins WR Chris Bell Skip to main content SI.COM Rookie wide receiver Chris Bell likely won't play for the Miami Dolphins against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 10, but the update on his status actually wasn't terrible news in the big picture. It's a setback of sorts, for sure, for the rookie third-round pick, but anytime we see Bell and knee on the injury report, there's reason for concern. It's overall been a tough rookie season for Bell, though he did surpass a lot of expectations by being ready for the start of the regular season. The production, however, has been very pedestrian. Bell has appeared in all eight games this season, but he's got only 12 catches for 148 yards for a 12.3-yard average with no touchdowns. Worse, he's been held without a catch three times, including during the 19-9 loss agianst the Detroit Lions last Sunday when he was targeted only once. On that pass attempt, Bell failed to get separation on a slant, an issue that's popped up regularly this season. Some of that, of course, could be attributed to Bell still working his way back after the knee injury. The hope, of course, is that Bell can finish with a flurry this season to possibly carry some momentum heading into 2027 because he did flash high-end potential in college. Bell's status was just one of the injury updates that Hafley provided Friday when he also indicated, as expected, that center Aaron Brewer will miss the Colts game because he's still in concussion protocol. Hafley confirmed that Andrew Meyer will take his place at center in the starting lineup. Tight end Will Kacmarek should be ready to go after missing practice Wednesday with quad and knee issues. This article originally appeared on Palm Beach Post: Dolphins injury report: QB Malik Willis, C Aaron Brewer out vs. Colts Miami Dolphins All-Pro center Aaron Brewer remains in concussion protocol and will not play against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Coach Jeff Hafley said Andrew Meyer will start in Brewer's place. Meyer, who started a game last season, has worked closely with Kyle McCord since the quarterback's arrival from Green Bay. McCord will be making his first NFL start in place of Malik Willis, who is on injured reserve. "He's done a nice job. Have a lot of confidence in Meyer," Hafley said. Hafley also said his new quarterback has a "very calm confidence" about him. "He's got a quiet leadership about him. He's got a confidence to him. He's very calm in the huddle. And he seems to be grasping everything really well," Hafley said. "I think he's done a really good job in the two practices that we've had. (Friday's) a big day again, getting more in the red zone and polishing up some stuff. "But again, this will be a process, right? I'm not going to expect him to look perfect. There's going to be hopefully some really good moments for him and then there's going to be some that we're going to have to continue to grow in these next games. But I'm excited for him and I appreciate how he's worked, attacked the game plan and how he's kind of communicating and developing chemistry with the players around him in the huddle." "The way Chop's playing and really practicing, I think he's a great example of what it's supposed to look like," Hafley said. "And I think he's going to grow into one of those roles."

away.headline: Dolphins’ Brents returns to Indy; where impending free agent stands. Injury report
away.blurb: “Absolutely,” he said Thursday. “That’s been a big focal point for myself. Talking to the coaching staff, everybody knows I can play. I just need to stay healthy and available. I’m doing everything I can, whether with nutrition, getting extra treatment, making sure I’m healthy.” Indianapolis drafted Brents 44th overall out of Kansas State — where he was an All-Big 12 selection during his final season (2022). Does he want to prove to the Colts that they made a mistake? “No,” he said. “I’m exactly where I’m supposed to be. It was a blessing for me to be able to come out here to Miami. No bad blood. “Being back at home is going to be great because I have my family around. I have a lot of respect for the Colts; they gave me an opportunity to live out my dream. Mr. [Jim] Irsay, God rest his soul, gave me an opportunity to play in the National Football League.” As expected, the Dolphins ruled out center Aaron Brewer for Sunday’s game. He remains in concussion protocol. Receiver Chris Bell, who was hit in the knee during Wednesday’s practice, is doubtful, but Jeff Hafley said it’s not a longterm injury. Receiver Jared Wayne (quad) also is out Sunday. Those are the only three Dolphins players on the 53-man roster who have an injury designation for the Colts game. Cornerback Darrell Baker, who is on the PUP list, is questionable. The Dolphins have 18 more days to move Baker to the 53-man roster. Kenneth Grant, who have averaged only 22 defensive snaps per game in his four games back from a toe injury, said he’s ready to play significantly more in the absence of Zach Sieler, who’s out for the year with a torn biceps. “I’ve been leaning more toward that than tackle lately,” he said. “I’m a bigger body out there, going against tight ends, a bigger body than they’re used to.” Instead, the focus will remain what it has been all season: maximizing the skills that made him a 2023 second-round pick and proving to everyone that he can stay healthy. In his second season as a Dolphin, Brents has done a pretty good job of the first and a very good job of the second. After playing in just 18 of 51 games in his first three NFL seasons, Brents has appeared in all eight games this season and started five after missing a large chunk of preseason. On three occasions, he left during the game and then returned, twice because of stingers and once because of dehydration. Was returning to the games important to him to show he can be durable? Brents, who missed Miami’s final six games last season with a foot injury, was the team’s best cover corner during the first few games this year. He gave up 61 yards of receptions in the Patriots game but was very good last Sunday against Detroit. He’s making a case for the Dolphins to re-sign him, and defensive coordinator Sean Duggan this week named Brents as one of the team’s most improved players. “He’s a pleaser; he wants to make anyone in position of authority happy,” cornerbacks coach Jahmile Addae said this week. “He’s a tough kid.

away.headline: Travis Etienne’s Status for Saints-Panthers Comes Into Focus After Final Injury Report
away.blurb: Travis Etienne Jr. made it through a full week of practice, and the New Orleans Saints are leaving the door open for Sunday. The running back is listed as questionable on the final Week 10 injury report for the Saints’ game against the Carolina Panthers . Etienne was limited Wednesday and Thursday before practicing fully Friday, according to NBC Sports . He is still on injured reserve, so the Saints have to activate him by Saturday afternoon for him to play. Etienne hasn’t played since straining his left hamstring in the Week 3 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders . Coach Kellen Moore said Wednesday that he would let the week play out before deciding. If Etienne does return, New Orleans Football’s Nick Underhill expects the Saints to limit his snaps, as they did with rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson in his return from a hamstring injury last week. The rest of the report shows why the Saints could use him. Moore ruled out center Erik McCoy (biceps), right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee), running back C.J. Donaldson (shoulder) and defensive lineman Christen Miller (knee), per Saints Wire . Cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. is also questionable. Ravens reveal Lamar Jackson recovering from broken and dislocated thumb, out 'about 6-10 weeks' Chiefs' Kenneth Walker listed as questionable against Falcons after late injury report addition Entertainment Entertainment Home ··· Boxing By our count, Etienne’s 128 rushing yards still rank second on the team even though he has played in just three of the Saints’ eight games, according to ESPN . He averaged 4.3 yards on 30 carries before the injury, and quarterback Tyler Shough said this week, “I’m excited to have him back.” Losing two starters up front makes a healthy back even more valuable against a Panthers team the Saints are tied with atop the NFC South at 3-5. Our look at the Saints’ remaining schedule shows how much Sunday’s result matters. This article first appeared on Athlon Sports and was syndicated with permission. away.headline: Panthers admit unusual mistake involving injured RB Jonathon Brooks
away.blurb: The Panthers opened Brooks’ 21-day practice window to return from injured reserve on Wednesday, and he was listed as a full participant for Wednesday’s and Thursday’s practice sessions. Brooks, as well as cornerback Mike Jackson, took scout team reps and should have been listed as limited for both of those days. Both Brooks and Jackson were officially listed as doubtful for Sunday’s Week 10 matchup against the New Orleans Saints. Starting running back Chuba Hubbard has stepped up in a big way with Brooks unavailable. Through eight games this season, he has 619 rushing yards, five rushing touchdowns, 167 receiving yards and two receiving touchdowns — serving as the engine of the Panthers’ offense. Related Articles NFL Insider Explains Ravens’ Lamar Jackson Return Window Carolina Panthers running back Jonathon Brooks was placed on injured reserve after sustaining groin and core muscle injuries in Week 2 of the 2026 season, causing him to miss each of the last six games. But on Friday, a Panthers team spokesperson admitted those designations were a mistake. The Panthers’ running back depth chart is thin behind Hubbard, featuring Trevor Etienne, AJ Dillon and Anthony Tyus III. Carolina is 3-5 to begin their 2026 campaign, dropping each of their last three games. However, they still sit atop the NFC South standings — tied with the Saints. Sunday’s Week 10 clash against New Orleans will kick off at 1 p.m. ET. away.headline: Struggling Panthers could get 5 starters, 4 reserves back from injuries in the coming weeks
away.blurb: Carolina opened the 21-day practice windows on Wednesday for cornerback Mike Jackson, wide receiver Xavier Legette and running back Jonathon Brooks to return from injured reserve. Outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips, guard Damien Lewis and cornerback Will Lee III returned to practice after missing time with injuries, while versatile offensive lineman Brady Christensen entered his second week in the 21-day practice window and is nearing his return. Coach Dave Canales said it's too early in the week to know who'll be available for Sunday's road game against the Saints. The Panthers held a light practice on Wednesday, and Canales said he should know more later in the week once the medical staff is able to evaluate the injured players' progress. The Panthers are also hopeful to get left tackle Ickey Ekwonu and cornerback Jaycee Horn back in the coming weeks. That’s five starters — Jackson, Phillips, Lewis, Ekwonu and Horn — and four key reserves potentially returning for the stretch run. The Panthers (3-5) needed some good news. They've lost three straight, although they remain tied with New Orleans for first place in the NFC South. Tampa Bay and Atlanta, both 3-6, are lurking right behind in a division that any team can win if it can just, well, win. “The guys who can help us right now, we will have them up,” Canales said. One of the reasons the Panthers were so quiet at the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday is that they have so many players returning from injuries, Canales said. “I'm excited about the guys that we have that are staring right at us and are going to come back to us in whatever order that may look like,” Canales said. “We feel really strong about this group and I have a lot of confidence in the guys that we have in this locker room.” Jackson, in particular, could provide a boost this week. Carolina's secondary has been hit hard with Jackson and Horn missing the last five games. With Lee and Akayleb Evans also hurt, Carolina was down to starting its fifth and sixth cornerbacks — Marco Wilson and Corey Thornton — on Sunday against the Denver Broncos. picks.blurb: Pick Six: Buffalo Bills at New York Jets - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Commanders edge Giants Skattebo's spooky stare 'Who Let the Dogs Out'? It's official: Poch to Man United Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Pick Six: Buffalo Bills at New York Jets ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - JANUARY 04: Running back Ray Davis #22 of the Buffalo Bills runs the ball during the fourth quarter against the New York Jets at Highmark Stadium on January 04, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. The Bills defeated the Jets 35-8. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bent Double · SB Nation Fri, November 13, 2026 at 4:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Jets will be a home underdog against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, having lost seven of their last eight games. Other than a last-gasp loss to the Patriots in week four, the Bills' record is unblemished this year. Surely the Jets can't pull off an upset, can they? Here are six storylines to watch as New York seeks to flip their season on its head: It's a trap! America is already looking ahead to the Bills-Chiefs game scheduled to take place in the evening of Thanksgiving Thursday. While Buffalo has two games to play between now and then, they will feel good about their chances of still only having one loss after playing the Jets this week and Miami next week. Kansas City has lost just twice so this could be decisive in the race for the AFC's top seed. We've seen situations like this before though. While the Jets are rarely the team to take advantage of the opportunity, their profile as a team that has kept a lot of games close and come up just short in the end could make them dangerous if the Bills get complacent. And if they did get complacent, who could blame them? After all, the last time these teams met, the Bills rested all of their starters and still won 35-8. Then again, that was a very different Jets team too. The only current non-offensive line starters who started that game are Harrison Phillips, Jamien Sherwood and Adonai Mitchell. Can Mitchell bounce back? It's become traditional this year to have at least one high profile player that doesn't get the ball on offense. Last week, it was Adonai Mitchell, a player who seven days earlier, had posted the best numbers of his career. The Jets really seem to be struggling with the whole "many mouths to feed" aspect of having provided their quarterback with an adequate number of pass catching weapons for the first time in several seasons. However, Mitchell not seeing the ball last week was not for the want of trying as he was thrown to seven times. Opening drive success We could easily spend column inches here talking about why the Jets can't convert in the red zone, or how they shouldn't abandon the running game, or when are they ever going to intercept another pass, but how about we discuss something they have actually been doing well? For each of the past five games, the Jets have driven downfield and scored on their opening possession, which has played a big part in them still being competitive heading into the second half of each game. So, now we have to ask the question – can this continue? And…how will the team react if it doesn't? This isn't the first time in recent memory that the offensive has looked good early on in games, and executed the scripted part of the gameplan effectively, only to then go on to struggle in the second half when points are needed to convert wins. Back in 2020, where Adam Gase's Jets were in danger of going winless until very late in the season, they actually scored eight times in a row on their opening drive. The current decision makers would ideally not like to have too many similarities to that 2020 team. Gregory Rousseau's ascent to super-stardom The biggest threat on the Bills defense is obviously edge rusher Gregory Rousseau, who is having a monster year. After just eight games, Rousseau has already tied his career-high with eight sacks, while also doubling his career mark for passes defensed with another eight. Rousseau primarily lines up on the left, so it will be mostly up to Armand Membou to try and keep him quiet. Rousseau had a two sack game against the Jets in his second season in 2022, but surprisingly otherwise only has one sack in eight other games against the Jets. The Bills are 7-2 in these matchups, though. Having not been traded, is Will McDonald's role going to change? The Jets opted not to trade former first round pick Will McDonald during the week, despite reports of interest from a number of teams. Head coach Aaron Glenn has been suggesting McDonald is still very much in the Jets plans for the rest of this season, and he is of course under contract for next year after New York exercised his fifth year option. He even implied McDonald had earned a bigger role. McDonald's defensive snap count percentage has dropped from 66% in both 2024 and 2025 to just 46% in 2026 and, even more confoundingly, his percentage of run snaps has increased. Will an increase in playing time for McDonald happen on Sunday? And, if it does, are we destined to see diminishing returns in regard to his production? What's the plan for the secondary? A matchup against the team with the number one offense in the entire NFL is not really the ideal time to experiment with line-up changes but the Jets are desperately striving for more consistency from their back seven, in addition to having an undermanned front that is struggling to stop the run. Having missed a meeting and made some on-field mistakes, the previous starting slot corner – Jarvis Brownlee Jr. – is in the doghouse. However, rookie D'Angelo Ponds has looked overmatched at times which is hardly surprising given how he is learning a new position and missed half of training camp. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Buffalo Bills (7-1) visit the New York Jets (2-7) on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium, with the AFC East rivals heading in dramatically different directions. Buffalo sits three games clear of second-place New England atop the division while the Jets have lost four in a row and sit but a half-game out of the cellar in the AFC East. The Bills enter the week with the NFL’s highest-scoring offense at 32.0 points per game and lead the league with 386.4 yards per game, powered by Josh Allen and a rushing attack featuring James Cook III . The Jets, meanwhile, are averaging just 20.2 points per game which begs the question: Can Geno Smith and the Jets score enough to keep up with the Bills’ elite attack? Working in the Jets’ favor is that Buffalo has a short turnaround after grinding out a 23-6 road victory over the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night. It was a far more physical game than the final score suggests. The Bills managed just three points on their first six possessions, and Allen threw an early interception, but his 25-yard touchdown pass to Keleki Latu with 44 seconds remaining in the first half gave Buffalo a 10-6 advantage. From there the Bills wore down Minnesota, holding the ball for an extraordinary 42:32 and running 79 offensive plays. Cook carried 31 times for 107 yards, including a five-yard fourth-quarter touchdown, while Allen finished 21-of-31 for 234 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Buffalo’s defense was even better, limiting Minnesota to 178 total yards and nine first downs while forcing three turnovers. The Jets return home after a 35-12 loss at Kansas City. Despite an early 6-0 lead, New York’s offensive woes were impossible to ignore. Smith and co. repeatedly stalled and had to settle for four Jason Sanders field goals. The Chiefs led just 14-12 at halftime before completely controlling the second half. New York finished with only 229 yards, went 2-for-12 on third down and failed to score a touchdown, while Smith completed 18 of 32 passes for 165 yards and was sacked five times. Breece Hall returned from a five-game absence caused by a quadriceps injury and produced 87 yards from scrimmage, while rookie Omar Cooper Jr. led the Jets with eight catches for 58 yards. Recent history adds another challenge for New York. Buffalo has won eight of the past 10 meetings, including a couple smacks last season, beating the Jets 30-10 at MetLife Stadium on Sept. 14, 2025 and 35-8 in Buffalo on Jan. 4, 2026. The Jets, on a four-game losing streak, welcome in the Buffalo Bills , who are 7-1 and currently the No. 1 seed in the AFC coming off Monday night's impressive 23-6 victory on the road over the Minnesota Vikings . Like most opponents, the Jets have failed to keep up with the Bills in recent meetings. Gang Green has dropped five straight games against Buffalo and have been outscored, 160-58, in the process. The Bills have averaged 32 points per game over that time and the Jets have been unable to score 21 or more points in any of those contests. It'll be another uphill battle for the Jets, who were swept by the Bills in 2026, with Buffalo winning by three or more scores both times last season. The Raiders have one of the worst defenses in the NFL, particularly when it comes to stopping the run. It's been a challenging rookie season for the first-round pick, who has yet to find his footing in Seattle's backfield. However, this matchup could be exactly what he needs to change the trajectory of his season. The Raiders have struggled mightily against opposing running backs, and Price should have opportunities to make an impact. With Zach Charbonnet also back in the backfield, Seattle has more options to attack Las Vegas. It is expected Price will take advantage of his opportunities and finally get that first NFL touchdown. That is not the kind of production we've grown accustomed to seeing from one of the NFL's best wide receivers. I expect a much different performance against Las Vegas. The Raiders have struggled to contain opposing offenses. I think he gets back to dominating opposing secondaries. Bold Prediction No. 2: Seahawks' rushing attack finally has a monster game The Raiders are allowing a league-leading 151.2 rushing yards per game. That's an invitation for Seattle to establish its ground game and take advantage of one of the NFL's worst run defenses. Seattle averages 110 yards on the ground. The Seahawks have yet to consistently get their rushing attack going, but this is the perfect opportunity to change that. With rookie Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet back from injury, Seattle has the personnel to make life miserable for Las Vegas. It shouldn't matter who is getting the carries. I expect the Seahawks to pound the rock throughout the afternoon and finish with close to 200 rushing yards. And remember, I still expect Smith-Njigba to have a monster game through the air. Seattle could realistically finish with more than 450 total yards of offense if everything goes according to plan. Bold Prediction No. 1: Fernando Mendoza has a nightmare game in his first NFL start Welcome to the NFL, Fernando Mendoza . The rookie quarterback is getting his first opportunity to lead the Raiders after the organization made a major change at the position. Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings . Unfortunately, his first start comes against a Seahawks defense that can make life extremely difficult for opposing quarterbacks. Mendoza does have some talented tight ends to work with, but Las Vegas' receiving corps is underwhelming. Seattle should be able to make things uncomfortable for the rookie, particularly if its pass rush can consistently generate pressure. It wouldn't be surprising if Mendoza throws a touchdown pass at some point. However, I expect the Raiders' offense to struggle for most of the afternoon. The prediction is that Mendoza finishes with fewer than 175 passing yards and completes less than 65% of his attempts. His first NFL start will be a difficult learning experience, and Seattle's defense will be the biggest reason why. picks.headline: Seahawks vs. Raiders, NFL Week 10 preview: Seattle’s ground game has a big opportunity
picks.blurb: Seahawks vs. Raiders, NFL Week 10 preview: Seattle’s ground game has a big opportunity - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Commanders edge Giants Skattebo's spooky stare 'Who Let the Dogs Out'? It's official: Poch to Man United Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Alexandre Castro · SB Nation Fri, November 13, 2026 at 5:20 PM UTC · 9 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Seattle Seahawks have an opportunity to exploit one of the Las Vegas Raiders' biggest weaknesses this Sunday. Las Vegas has struggled to establish its own ground game, while its defense has been among the NFL's worst at stopping the run. For Seattle, the path to controlling this game starts up front, on both sides of the ball. But the matchup is more complicated than the numbers might suggest. The Seahawks have struggled to run the ball consistently themselves, and the Raiders still have enough talent to punish an offense that becomes predictable. With Drew Lock dealing with an oblique/elbow injury and Sam Darnold sidelined, Seattle may need to lean even more heavily on its ground game and quick passing concepts. The ground game could decide this matchup The Raiders are averaging just 71.3 rushing yards per game and 2.9 yards per carry through nine games. Ashton Jeanty has 362 rushing yards on 114 attempts, averaging 3.2 yards per carry. He has actually produced more yards as a receiver, with 371 yards on 42 catches. Mike Washington Jr. has been more efficient on the ground, averaging 3.9 yards per carry on 71 attempts for 275 yards. He gives Las Vegas another option, but neither back has helped establish a reliable rushing attack. That creates an opportunity for Seattle's defense. The Seahawks have allowed just 78.8 rushing yards per game over their last five contests, including consecutive performances against Kansas City and Arizona in which they surrendered only 50 rushing yards. Chicago, however, ran for 126 yards and three touchdowns against Seattle on November 2, showing that the defense remains vulnerable when an opponent finds ways to create movement at the line of scrimmage and attacking the edges. The Raiders have struggled to create that movement themselves. Seattle should be able to challenge Jeanty and Washington early, force Las Vegas into unfavorable down-and-distance situations, and make rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza carry more of the offensive burden. Can Seattle take advantage of the Raiders' weakness on the other side of the ball? Las Vegas is allowing 151.2 rushing yards per game and five yards per carry, both league-worst figures. That is a significant opportunity for a Seahawks offense that has averaged 110.8 rushing yards per game this season, although Seattle's 3.9 yards per carry shows that consistency has been an issue. Zach Charbonnet's return offers some reason for optimism. In his second game back from an ACL injury, Charbonnet led Seattle with 77 rushing yards on 16 carries against Arizona. Jadarian Price added 24 yards on nine carries, along with four catches for 54 receiving yards. Their contributions helped Seattle put together a more effective ground attack last week. Sunday will be their third game together this season, giving the Seahawks another opportunity to build on that progress. The offensive line, however, remains central to the equation. Seattle's struggles cannot be pinned entirely on its running backs. The unit has struggled to consistently create movement, and injuries have forced changes across the line. The return of Charbonnet helps, but even the best running backs need room to work. That balance run vs pass matters even more this week. With Lock managing an additional oblique injury, Seattle has good reason to emphasize quick throws and a strong running game rather than repeatedly asking its quarterback to hold the ball and make difficult downfield reads. If the Seahawks can establish the run, they can dictate the pace, protect their quarterback, and keep Maxx Crosby from becoming the defining factor in the game. Brock Bowers is the biggest threat in the passing game Despite missing two games, Bowers has recorded 48 receptions for 658 yards and six touchdowns in seven appearances. That translates to 94 receiving yards per game, with an average of ten targets per contest. Those are outstanding numbers for a tight end, particularly one who has already demonstrated the ability to produce against different defensive looks. Bowers also brings positional versatility. He can line up as a traditional tight end, move into the slot, align outside. That flexibility forces defenses to adjust their personnel and assignments before the snap. When Bowers lines up inside, linebackers and safeties may be responsible for covering him. When he moves outside, cornerbacks can be forced into difficult matchups. His alignment can also create opportunities for Las Vegas to isolate him against a defender it believes it can exploit. The challenge does not end when the ball arrives. Bowers is dangerous after the catch, capable of turning a short completion into a significant gain. Seattle must therefore do more than simply keep him in front of the defense. Tackling and closing throwing windows will be just as important as the initial coverage. The Seahawks have shown they can limit tight ends by keeping the ball in front of them and preventing additional yards after the catch. The first matchup with Arizona's Trey McBride provides a useful recent example to study. Seattle allowed McBride to get involved as a receiver, but limited his yard production. The Seahawks have had strong stretches defending tight ends, but spacing in the underneath zones remains an area to monitor. Bowers is precisely the kind of player who can find those spaces, settle into soft spots in coverage, and force defenders to make difficult tackles. Seattle cannot afford to lose track of him when the Raiders use motion or change his alignment. Communication before the snap will be critical, especially if Las Vegas tries to force a linebacker into coverage against Bowers. The other weapons: Tre Tucker and Michael Mayer Bowers is the centerpiece, but the Raiders have other receiving options capable of making Seattle pay if the defense concentrates too heavily on the tight end. Tre Tucker is the most obvious threat downfield. He has 33 receptions for 529 yards and four touchdowns, averaging 16 yards per catch. His 58.8 receiving yards per game and ability to stretch the field make him an important part of the Raiders' passing attack. Michael Mayer is another player to watch. The second tight end has 39 receptions for 388 yards and a touchdown. His presence becomes particularly important when the Raiders deploy two-tight-end formations, allowing them to create different combinations of blocking and receiving threats. Jeanty also remains a receiving threat out of the backfield, adding another player Seattle must account for in underneath coverage. Protecting Drew Lock and handling Maxx Crosby Seattle's offensive line faces a difficult test against Crosby, one of the league's most disruptive edge defenders. He has four sacks this season, but his impact extends beyond the sack total. His ability to generate pressure, attack the quarterback's launch point, and disrupt plays makes him dangerous even when he does not finish with a takedown. The Raiders have recorded 19 sacks as a team, with Kwity Paye and Malcolm Koonce contributing three apiece. Crosby is the headliner, but Seattle cannot afford to focus exclusively on him and leave the other rushers with favorable opportunities. Seattle may therefore need to favor quicker reads, shorter throws, and a greater emphasis on getting the ball out before the pass rush arrives once Lock has elbow and oblique injury. That approach also makes sense against Crosby. The longer the quarterback holds the ball, the more time the Raiders' pass rush has to create pressure. Quick throws can neutralize some of that advantage, particularly if Seattle can pair them with an effective running game. The Seahawks have also shown that they can avoid sacks when their protection and decision-making work together. Lock has taken only two sacks in his three appearances this season, despite attempting 76 passes. Seattle should continue to use that approach rather than repeatedly asking its offensive line to hold up against Crosby in obvious passing situations. If the Seahawks can remain ahead of the chains, use play-action effectively, and avoid predictable third-and-long situations, they will have a better chance of keeping the pass rush under control. Fernando Mendoza faces Mike Macdonald On the other side of the ball, the Seahawks have a chance to make life difficult for another rookie quarterback. Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, has been named the Raiders' starting quarterback following Kirk Cousins' trade to Minnesota. Mendoza has appeared in just one regular-season game, completing six of eight passes for 48 yards against New England. Sunday will be his first NFL start. That is a significant challenge against Mike Macdonald's defense. Seattle entered Week 10 ranked among the league's best defenses, and its performance against Arizona was particularly impressive. The Seahawks held the Cardinals to three points, 50 rushing yards, and 166 passing yards while recording three sacks. Macdonald has shown that he is willing to change his approach when personnel limitations demand it. Against Arizona, Seattle used an unusually aggressive pressure plan, with blitzes. The Seahawks were dealing with several significant absences, including Leonard Williams and Uchenna Nwosu, and the added pressure helped compensate for a reduced pass-rush rotation. It would not be surprising to see Seattle continue using simulated pressures, disguised coverages, and different blitz looks against Mendoza. The objective would not necessarily be to send extra rushers on every passing down, but to make the rookie identify the defense, recognize where pressure is coming from, and process his reads quickly. That is particularly important for a quarterback making his first start. A defense that disguises its intentions can force hesitation, disrupt timing, and create opportunities for pressure before the play has time to develop. Final Thoughts This matchup brings together two coaches who know each other's football philosophies well. Kubiak spent the 2025 season with Seattle. Their time together means each understands something about the other's approach, tendencies, and preferred ways of attacking an opponent. Macdonald has spoken about the challenges Kubiak's offense presented during their practices together. But familiarity only goes so far. The Seahawks still need to execute, protect their quarterback, and avoid allowing Crosby to dictate the game. Defensively, they must contain Bowers, keep Tucker from generating explosive plays, and make Mendoza prove he can consistently beat an NFL defense. This should not be an easy game, especially with Seattle managing injuries. But if the Seahawks have genuine postseason ambitions, these are the kinds of matchups they need to win. The opportunity is there; now they have to take it.

To add another element to this matchup, Fernando Mendoza will make his first career start on Sunday. With that in mind, here are predictions for the Raiders' top offensive players against Seattle. Fernando Mendoza Projected Stat Line: 20-of-32 for 235 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions As mentioned, the No. 1 overall pick is making his NFL debut on Sunday. Because of Las Vegas' porous offensive line, Kubiak will likely deploy quick passes to get the ball out of Mendoza's hands as quickly as possible. Mendoza needs the run game to open up passing lanes. Besides winning this game, making Mendoza as comfortable as possible should be Kubiak's main objective. That also increases the chances the Raiders pull off the upset. Ashton Jeanty Stat Line Projection: 12 carries for 45 yards; four receptions for 26 yards To say the second-year running back has struggled this season would be an understatement. Jeanty hasn't surpassed 27 rushing yards in each of the last five games. If the 22-year-old running back struggles against the Bills and 49ers, Jeanty is facing an uphill battle to produce his first productive outing in weeks. Now, Mendoza's mobility could open up rushing lanes for Jeanty. Nevertheless, the Boise State product has to be better. He hasn't lived up to the "generational talent" tag when he first entered the 2025 NFL Draft. Stat Line Projection: eight receptions for 75 yards and one touchdown Bowers was the primary target in the first nine games, and that will be amplified with Mendoza under center. The rookie quarterback has shown the ability to go through progressions cleanly, but the star tight end will likely be his first read on most dropbacks. The 23-year-old tight end is averaging nearly 10 targets, 6.8 receptions, and 94 yards per game. Bowers' production should mirror those season-long averages, despite facing one of the best defenses in the league. picks.blurb: Seahawks vs. Raiders Week 10 tracker: Injury updates, prediction, storylines and more - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search News Finance More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Scores / Schedules Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald is seen before a game | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Lee Vowell · 12th Man Rising Thu, November 12, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads About our Ads The Seattle Seahawks are 5-4 and head to Las Vegas to play the 4-5 Raiders at Allegiant Stadium in Week 10. Seattle will be playing with a backup quarterback, Drew Lock, and Las Vegas will have a rookie quarterback, Fernando Mendoza, in his first career start. Head coach Mike Macdonald's team still has the better roster, and should be expected to win, but the Raiders are better this season than in quite some time. A victory against Seattle would be huge for their collective confidence. Health could be a factor. Seattle's injury report was fairly lengthy, so even some players who perform in Week 10 might not be close to 100 percent. At least, the bye week follows in Week 11. Seattle Seahawks injury updates for Week 10 Anthony Bradford Charles Cross Ribs and quad Elbow and oblique Quenton Nelson Uchenna Nwosu Patrick O'Connell Connor O'Toole Personal matter Rashid Shaheed Jaxon Smith-Njigba Leonard Williams Sam Darnold has already been ruled out, so he won't play. Drew Lock was expected to be limited all week, but is expected to play in Week 10. Leonard Williams is already trending toward missing another game. He will be missed. Seattle will announce its full list of inactives an hour and a half before kickoff, and this article will be updated with the latest information. Raiders inactives and injury updates Thomas Booker Foley Fatukasi Shoulder and back Trey Zuhn III The Raiders are fairly healthy, but what doesn't show on their injury report is the trade of quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings. This means rookie Fernando Mendoza will start for the first time in the NFL. As with Seattle, Vegas will announce its inactives an hour and a half before kickoff. How to watch Seahawks vs. Raiders in Week 10 Date: Sunday, November 15 Time: 1:05 p.m. PT TV Network: CBS (KIRO 7 in Seattle) Announcers: Ian Eagle (play-by-play), Ross Tucker (analysis), and Evan Washburn (sideline reporter) In the Seattle area, you can also stream the game on NFL+, while nationally, you might need a subscription to YouTube TV's NFL Sunday Ticket to stream or watch the game. You can listen to the game on the Seahawks Mobile App, SiriusXM channels 123 or 269, Seattle Sports 710 AM, and KIRO Newsradio 97.3. Steve Raible will provide the play-by-play for the Seahawks broadcast, while Dave Wyman will do the analysis, and Jen Mueller will report from the sidelines. Storylines to watch for Seahawks in Week 10 How will Fernando Mendoza do? Obviously, what most national fans will be interested in is how well the No. 1 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft will do in his first career start . While Vegas trading Kirk Cousins made sense, Mendoza's first two starts couldn't come against tougher defenses: The Seahawks and then the Denver Broncos. Presumably, head coach Klint Kubiak isn't going to let Mendoza throw the ball 50 times, but he could have a somewhat conservative game plan to operate with. Kubiak is a good coach, so fans should expect a difficult challenge, even against a rookie quarterback. Will Drew Lock succeed against a non-Arizona Cardinals team? The difference between Lock games and Sam Darnold games has been significant this season. Lock has turned the ball over in three games. Darnold has nine interceptions in six games. What fans have seen from Lock might not be reality, though. He played the majority of reps in Week 1 against the New England Patriots, but Week 1s are often lies. His other two games have been against the terrible Cardinals. Darnold has faced far tougher competition. Lock's true first test might come against the Raiders, who are eighth in the league with seven interceptions. Can the Seahawks succeed running the ball? Week 9 against the Cardinals looked quite a bit different offensively for Seattle. That is partly because running backs Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price were healthier. To win with Lock, and even when Darnold returns, the running game needs to continue being good. The Raiders are tight for last in the NFL at allowing 5.0 yards per carry. They are also last in yards allowed per rushing attempt at 151.2. The Seahawks must run the ball effectively to win. Prediction for Week 10 Seahawks 21, Raiders 14 This game is difficult to predict due to a number of factors, including how good Mendoza might be and the overall health of the Seahawks' defense. If Leonard Williams and Uchenna Nwosu miss the game again, the normally lofty standard of Mike Macdonald's defense could be exposed by a good offensive coach for Las Vegas. The hope is that Seattle wins a fairly ugly game, one that will probably be close until the end. Hopefully, Drew Lock just plays another clean game. The only other changes were that tight end AJ Barner , who was a full participant Wednesday with a finger injury, has been removed from the injury report altogether, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who got a rest day on Wednesday, was a full participant. As expected, quarterback Drew Lock was limited again, as has been the plan as he prepares to start while dealing with elbow and oblique injuries. Receiver Rashid Shaheed , who is trying to make his way back from a knee injury that kept him out of two games, was a full participant for the second day in a row, while Uchenna Nwosu , who is trying to get back from an ankle injury, was limited for the second day in a row. Defensive tackle Leonard Williams , who is dealing with a stinger, was a non-participant for the second day in a row, as were quarterback Sam Darnold and left guard Quenton Nelson , both of whom have already been ruled out of Week 10 by Mike Macdonald. For the Raiders, defensive tackle Folorunso Fatukasi (shoulder, back) was upgraded from limited to full participation, while defensive tackle Thomas Booker (ankle) and offensive lineman Trey Zuhn (concussion) were limited for the second straight day. The Seahawks kicked off their practice week on Wednesday ahead of a Week 10 road matchup against the Raiders, and saw a couple of players who missed Sunday's win over the Cardinals return to the practice field. Receiver Rashid Shaheed , who has missed the last two games with a knee injury, was a full participant, while outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu , who has also missed two games with an ankle injury, was a limited participant. Quarterback Drew Lock , who is expected to start in place of Darnold for the second straight week, was limited, as expected, due to elbow and oblique injuries. Lock was limited over the previous three weeks due to the elbow injury, then picked up the oblique injury in Sunday's game. Seahawks Injury Report Paints a Troubling Picture for Many Players
away.blurb: Do the Seattle Seahawks need all hands on deck to beat a heavily-wounded Arizona Cardinals squad this upcoming weekend? We’re about to find out the hard way, because after Friday’s report, it’s clear they will have many hands not on deck. While I don’t believe it’s sufficient to excuse a loss, it’s fair to say this week is about survival more than anything else. Let’s not bury the lead here. The Seahawks have six starters out for this one. Sam Darnold (ribs, quadricep), Rashid Shaheed (knee), Charles Cross (ankle), Quenton Nelson (knee), Leonard Williams (stinger), and Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) will be sidelined this week, which is a lot to swallow for any team. home.headline: Seattle Seahawks Get Great Rashid Shaheed News Before Raiders Game
home.blurb: Shaheed's return is not official, but practicing without limitations to begin the week puts him in a considerably better position than he was entering Seattle's 17-3 victory over the Arizona Cardinals on November 8. Rashid Shaheed Takes Major Step Toward Seahawks Return Shaheed has been sidelined for two consecutive games, leaving Seattle without one of its most explosive offensive weapons and an important contributor in the return game. His full participation Wednesday marks a substantial improvement from last week, when he remained out of practice before ultimately being ruled out against Arizona. Having Shaheed available would give Lock another dangerous option in the passing game and provide Seattle with additional flexibility on special teams. Shaheed's possible return also comes after rookie running back Jadarian Price handled kickoff-return responsibilities against Arizona while Seattle was dealing with injuries. There is still an important distinction between returning to practice and being cleared for a game. Shaheed must make it through the remainder of the week, but Wednesday's report offered the clearest positive indication yet that he is progressing toward a return. Seattle received another encouraging update on outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu, who participated on a limited basis after also missing the past two games with an ankle injury. The situation is more concerning for Seattle's offensive line, where Cross and Nelson remain sidelined. Macdonald has already ruled Nelson out for Sunday after the veteran guard underwent a minor knee procedure earlier this week. “I'd say we haven't ruled anybody out yet, but I think everybody needs to make progress,” Macdonald said, according to Seahawks.com . Meanwhile, Lock was limited Wednesday with right elbow and oblique injuries. The quarterback suffered the oblique injury during the Cardinals game after entering the matchup with an existing elbow issue. Macdonald nevertheless expects Lock to start against Las Vegas, with Darnold targeting a possible return following Seattle's Week 11 bye. home.blurb: Seahawks-Raiders Wednesday injury report: Leonard Williams still out, Rashid Shaheed returns - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL 'Who Let the Dogs Out'? Seattle released the first of the three weekly injury reports, which is headlined by the health of backup quarterback Drew Lock, who is battling a lingering elbow injury and a new oblique injury. Lock was limited in practice on Wednesday, with head coach Mike Macdonald indicating that the veteran is "making good progress" and may start against the Raiders. Whoever is under center will once again be working with a patchwork offensive line as stars Quenton Nelson and Charles Cross did not practice. Nelson is battling a knee injury that might hold him out for his second straight game while Cross has been out with an ankle injury since Week 7. Backup guard Anthony Bradford continues to be hampered by a knee injury and was limited on Wednesday. On the defensive side, Leonard Williams remains out with a stinger that he suffered against the Kansas City Chiefs, and edge rusher Derick Hall was limited with a new back injury. Both would be a massive loss for the Seahawks front that will hope to ruin Raiders' rookie Fernando Mendoza's debut. It wasn't all negative for the Seahawks' defense, though, as signs are trending positive for edge rusher Uchenna Nwosu, who was limited with the ankle injury that's held him out of the team's last two games. It's official: Poch to Man United Jack Freeman · SB Nation Thu, November 12, 2026 at 12:29 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Seattle Seahawks emerged victorious in an injury bowl against the Arizona Cardinals last week, and it appears they may have to do it again on Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders. The ominous messaging leaves the entirety of Seattle on Jalen Milroe watch yet again as the second-year player is the only other healthy quarterback on the Seahawks' 53-man roster and would come in if Lock couldn't play. The Seahawks offense appears to have a weapon returning as wide receiver and kicker returner Rashid Shaheed was a full participant in practice. Shaheed has had a quiet 2026, but remains a key piece to unlocking the Seahawks' offense as the organization is hopeful he emerges as a second option beside Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Meanwhile, the Raiders report was considerably smaller, so it appears they'll be near full-go against their former AFC West rival. For the Seahawks, they will have two more days of practice before setting game designations, so here's to hoping that the report shrinks throughout the week.

Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The favorites in August to claim the Lombardi Trophy, the LA Rams (5-4) currently sit on the wrong side of the playoff bubble as they prepare to take on the Arizona Cardinals (3-6) Sunday in Glendale. The Rams’ struggles are the result of injuries and consistently inconsistent play. That said, they take the field riding a three-game winning streak that has pushed them into a tie with Seatle for second in the NFC West. The Cardinals are last in the division as a result of losses two of the last three weeks. Los Angeles has climbed back into the playoff chase behind Matthew Stafford , who has thrown for 2,374 yards and 16 touchdowns. Arizona averages only 19.8 points per game while surrendering 28.3, but there is one significant reason the Rams won’t take the Cardinals lightly: Arizona already beat them 18-16 on Oct. 18 at SoFi Stadium. Los Angeles extended its winning streak to three last Sunday with a 20-13 road victory over the Washington Commanders. The Rams’ defense has been central to the turnaround, holding the Chargers to nine points and Washington to 13 in consecutive weeks, and Los Angeles enters Sunday allowing only 20.1 points and 312.9 yards per game. The major concern is what Stafford will have around him. Star receiver Puka Nacua , the team’s leading receiver with 715 yards, is out after suffering knee and toe injuries, while Davante Adams remains on injured reserve with a hamstring injury and tight end Terrance Ferguson is also sidelined. It is up to Head Coach Sean McVay and Stafford to keep the offense functioning even with several of its most important weapons sidelined. Arizona’s most recent outing was far less encouraging. The Cardinals followed up a thrilling and improbable 33-30 overtime win in Dallas with a 17-3 loss at Seattle. The Cardinals are now 3-6 and, remarkably, 0-3 at home, while an offense already struggling for consistency is undergoing a major change at quarterback. With Gardner Minshew placed on injured reserve, rookie Carson Beck is set to make his first appearance against the Rams, putting even more importance on running back Tyler Allgeier and tight end Trey McBride , who leads Arizona with 598 receiving yards and five touchdown catches. The recent history makes this matchup particularly interesting because as noted earlier, Arizona has already pulled off one of the season’s bigger divisional upsets. On Oct. 18, the Cardinals went into SoFi Stadium and beat the Rams 18-16 despite failing to score a touchdown, riding six field goals from Chad Ryland . Los Angeles took a 16-15 lead with 46 seconds remaining on a Stafford touchdown pass to Colby Parkinson , only for Arizona to drive back into field-goal range and win on Ryland’s 43-yarder as time expired. That result interrupted what had otherwise been a Rams-dominated stretch in the rivalry: Los Angeles beat Arizona 45-17 in December 2025 and 37-20 in January 2026, and the Rams lead the complete series 53-42-2, including a 2-0 postseason record. away.headline: Puka Nacua Injury Update, Latest News on Rams WR's Status and Return Timeline Amid Knee Issue
away.blurb: Ultimately, the Rams are not going to be nearly as dangerous with both Nacua and Adams out. After all, Los Angeles is three games behind the San Francisco 49ers in the NFC West at 5-4 and on the outside of the playoff picture looking in at this point. The Green Bay Packers have the final wild-card spot at 6-3 and will face the Rams in Week 12 while Nacua is still out. The Los Angeles Rams will be without wide receiver Puka Nacua for the foreseeable future. The NFC West team placed the playmaker on injured reserve because of his MCL injury. What's more, head coach Sean McVay said his expectation is Nacua will miss "extended time." This is a change in direction for the Rams, as McVay initially told reporters that even though the wide receiver was going to miss "a significant period of time," the plan was not to place him on IR due to "semantics with the roster." Losing Nacua is quite the blow for Los Angeles seeing how Davante Adams is already sidelined with a hamstring injury. Nacua's injury happened during Sunday's win over the Washington Commanders, although he still finished with a head-turning 14 receptions for 150 yards and one touchdown on 19 targets. Through seven games this season, he has 70 catches for 715 yards and four touchdowns. With both of Matthew Stafford's top receivers sidelined, the Rams will likely rely on the combination of Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield and CJ Daniels at the position. Tight end Tyler Higbee will likely see plenty of targets as well, although even he missed practice Thursday because of an illness. Nacua is one of the best wide receivers in the league and someone Stafford routinely targets double-digit amounts of time per game. There will be more pressure on the rushing attack to carry the offense with the two top playmakers sidelined, and there is also little room for error in the NFC standings. With remaining games against the Packers, 49ers and Kansas City Chiefs, as well as two against the Seattle Seahawks, there is a real chance the Rams will miss the playoffs. And those chances are much higher with Nacua not on the field.

away.headline: Rams' Myles Garrett expected to play at Arizona despite missing practice
away.blurb: LOS ANGELES (AP) — Los Angeles Rams defensive end Myles Garrett expects to play Sunday despite missing practice, while cornerback Trent McDuffie is questionable for their game at the Arizona Cardinals. Garrett was held out of practice on Friday after being limited earlier in the week because of a knee injury that caused him to miss seven games before returning to make three sacks with a forced fumble in the Rams’ 20-13 win at the Washington Commanders on Sunday. McDuffie is dealing with a back injury that forced him to miss the Rams’ third straight win last week, getting them over .500 for the first time this season at 5-4. McVay expressed optimism he would be able to play, provided McDuffie felt good coming out of Friday’s workout. The ongoing issues with the Rams’ two marquee offseason acquisitions is indicative of their larger injury crisis that has threatened a campaign that began with them as Super Bowl betting favorites. Los Angeles is so beat up that star wide receiver Puka Nacua was placed on injured reserve Thursday to free up a roster spot, a reversal from what McVay had indicated earlier in the week when he cited the limited number of IR slots remaining to be able to bring players back later in the season. “Some things changed where we needed that spot because of all the moving pieces,” said McVay, while adding that nothing has changed with the timeline for Nacua’s return from knee and toe injuries. Safety Kam Curl is questionable with a toe injury, but McVay indicated he is likely to play. The same is expected for the Rams’ banged-up crop of tight ends, Colby Parkinson (ribs), Tyler Higbee (illness) and Davis Allen (oblique). All three are needed to supplement the passing game with top receivers Nacua, Davante Adams (hamstring) and Jordan Whittington (back) on IR. Tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) and left guard Steve Avila (hamstring) were ruled officially out as was previously announced. “He’s had a really good week,” coach Sean McVay said. “Played a bunch of snaps, and expect him to be able to build on that. But we’re being smart with him.” Garrett was largely pleased with his performance, in which he played 61.5% of the defensive snaps, apart from needing to build up his endurance and address what he felt was a slow get-off time. “I'm sure Next Gen or PFF or somebody would tell me it wasn't too bad,” Garrett said. “It felt terrible to me.” “He was rolling, you know, doing a lot of good stuff yesterday,” McVay said. The Rams were upset by the Cardinals 18-16 on Oct. 18, giving up a last-minute drive which ended with Chad Ryland kicking his sixth field goal as time expired at SoFi Stadium. home.headline: Cardinals QB situation takes stunning turn with Gardner Minshew update: report
home.blurb: Following their 17-3 road loss Sunday to the Seattle Seahawks, the Arizona Cardinals received a major update on quarterback Gardner Minshew, who may have suffered a season-ending injury. On Monday evening, NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that Minshew “is feared to have suffered a torn UCL in his throwing arm.” Rapoport said Minshew suffered the injury before halftime but continued playing through it. According to Rapoport, Minshew will get additional testing done, but the injury could end his season and require a lengthy rehabilitation process. Minshew suffered the injury when he was hit by Seahawks pass rusher Dante Fowler while attempting a pass on the final play of the first half. The Cardinals quarterback grabbed his right arm after the rough hit, but continued to play. In Sunday’s game, Minshew completed 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards and was sacked three times by the Seahawks defense. Seattle held Arizona to just 198 total yards of offense for the game. More news: Chiefs HC Andy Reid Reveals Patrick Mahomes Injury Update Ahead of Falcons Game The devastating update arrived days after the team traded veteran starter Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens. Arizona’s unfortunate situation with Minshew has led to several developments, including Adam Schefter reporting that the team signed Josh Johnson off the Cincinnati Bengals’ practice squad. This is Johnson’s 15th team in 14 seasons. According to ESPN , in an initial report on the Cardinals’ injury updates, rookie Carson Beck was expected to start on Sunday. The Cardinals drafted the former Miami Hurricanes quarterback at No. 65 in the 3rd round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Beck led his team to the College Football Playoff National Championship game, which they lost to Fernando Mendoza and the Indiana Hoosiers. The decision to draft Beck was met with mixed reviews, with many sports outlets giving the team a low grade for the pick. NFL.com’s Chad Reuter graded Arizona’s Day 2 picks, including Beck, an “A,” indicating he had “a lot of big-game experience.” However, Reuter also noted that Beck’s decision-making was too inconsistent to be a “surefire starter.” Beck appeared in the NFL Hall of Fame Game this preseason against the Carolina Panthers, throwing for 188 yards and a touchdown in Arizona’s 33-30 loss. With ESPN reporting that Beck is expected to start Sunday, he’s poised to take over for a 3-6 Arizona team, unless they opt to use Johnson instead. Unfortunately, both quarterbacks could face a challenging matchup for the team’s next NFL game. The Cardinals host a Los Angeles Rams team on Sunday, Nov. 15, that has now won three straight games to improve to 5-4 for the season. The Rams also just got back the NFL Defensive Player of the Year, Myles Garrett, who recorded three sacks on Sunday in their 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders, so Beck or Johnson could face a difficult test for his first NFL start.
