home.headline: Cardinals Forced to Sign 40-Year-Old QB as Injuries Mount
home.blurb: “I think probably even stronger than how I said it yesterday. I wasn’t anticipating some of the things that we found out today. I knew that particularly on offense — (with) the defense there’s been a guy here and there, but there’s been some decent continuity over the last month, and I think you guys see that," LaFleur said. Cardinals Coach Said The Quiet Part Out Loud on Carson Beck ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals' Monday has taken a steep twist thanks to several significant injuries to their offense, and with news of Gardner Minshew potentially being done for the season, the organization has already targeted their next passer. From ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter: "With veteran QB Gardner Minshew sidelined due to a UCL injury, the Cardinals are signing QB Josh Johnson off the Bengals’ practice squad, per sources. The Cardinals will be Johnson’s 15th NFL team in 14 NFL seasons." Johnson, a perennial backup veteran quarterback, will be the team's No. 2 quarterback as the Cardinals prepare for their Week 10 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams — who just welcomed Myles Garrett back to the mix with a three-sack performance this Sunday. Minshew was injured on the final play of the second quarter against Seattle. He returned to finish the game but showed obvious discomfort. Rookie quarterback Carson Beck is slated to start for Arizona this week. Johnson, 40 years old, first entered the league as a fifth-round pick in the 2008 NFL Draft. He's played 50 NFL games with 11 starts, most recently starting twice for the Washington Commanders in 2025. In those two games, Johnson completed 34 of 54 passes for 372 yards for one touchdown and two interceptions. He has a 2-9 record as a starter. It was an extremely tough day for the Cardinals, who lost both Minshew and Michael Wilson . Arizona head coach Mike LaFleur says the team has to regroup, even amid the injuries. "I think you see 11 has won more and more each week, particularly over these last four weeks. Not the case on offense right now and that’s what I meant by that. There’s been a lot of moving parts, and I have to do a better job of stabilizing that to make sure that we don’t have performances like we did yesterday.” The Cardinals recently dealt Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens last week, thinning their quarterback room down to two. With Minshew injured, Beck was the only healthy quarterback on the roster prior to Johnson's signing. (Tom Fox/Dallas Morning News) SportsDay Staff · Dallas Morning News Fri, November 13, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Will the Cowboys finally be able to climb back to .500 and pick up their first marquee win of the season? They'll have a massive opportunity to do just that Sunday when the San Francisco 49ers come to AT&T Stadium as the two teams renew their historic rivalry . Dallas enters the game with a 4-5 record and, after the Commanders' win over the Giants on Thursday, a chance to climb even with New York in the win column. Meanwhile, San Francisco enters the game with a 7-1 record and has quickly established itself as one of the NFL's Super Bowl favorites. Can the Cowboys pull off an upset and get their season back on track? The Dallas Morning News ' columnists and beat writers gave their predictions below. Tim Cowlishaw The good news for Dallas is the 49ers can't really take advantage of the Cowboys' challenged secondary because of their injury troubles at wide receiver. The bad news is the 49ers can take advantage of everything else. A team that plays with grit despite its current 7-1 record, San Francisco figures to dominate time of possession with its multi-pronged running attack, and it will take some huge plays from Dak Prescott against the league's No. 3 defense to keep the Cowboys engaged for long in this one. The recipe is there for a Cowboys loss. The Cowboys haven't pieced together back-to-back wins in nearly a year, despite many opportunities along the way. The 49ers might be the class of the NFC, with an offense that continues to score, despite a ton of injuries, and a defense that is as fast as it is physical. Will this be the week the Cowboys finally stack two wins in a row? It's unlikely. 49ers 35, Cowboys 28 You won't find many (any?) realistic NFL fans giving the Cowboys a shot to win this week. Any path to victory would include the 49ers making self-inflicted mistakes and Dallas' offense playing flawlessly. Yes, the Cowboys' offense performs much better at AT&T Stadium, but it still disappears for long stretches during games. Even Brandon Aubrey has struggled to find his range of late. The red-clad fans will have plenty to cheer for in Arlington. Abraham Nudelstejer Given what we've seen this season, this is probably the easiest prediction to make so far. The Cowboys already have lost at home to a team whose season is all but over, and to another that could still reach the playoffs only because of the woeful state of its division. There is no tangible evidence of improvement that would justify picking Dallas to beat a squad that, with just one loss all year, appears destined to represent the NFC in the Super Bowl. The best Dallas can realistically hope for is to put up a spirited fight and begin preparing for next week's game. 49ers 34, Cowboys 13 Kevin Sherrington Jerry Jones did the right thing by not mortgaging any more of his future to try to save this season, and this game against the 49ers should do nothing but affirm that decision. The Cowboys won't hang 500 yards on the 49ers like they did the Colts. San Francisco has the third-best defense in the NFL, meaning Dak Prescott can't hope to outscore them. 49ers 31, Cowboys 24 Calvin Watkins If the postseason started today, the 49ers would be the No. 1 seed. The Cowboys? Well, you know what's happening with them. If the Cowboys want to get back into the playoff chase, and that's winning the NFC East, beating the 49ers is a good start. It's a difficult task considering how good the 49ers are on defense (ranked third in total defense) so the Cowboys' offense will have to be near-perfect. That's hard to do. The 49ers should handle things. 49ers 30, Cowboys 17 This article originally published at Expert predictions for Cowboys-49ers: Can Dallas climb to .500 with a huge upset? .

It's official: Poch to Man United Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies 49ers vs. Cowboys bold predictions for NFL Week 10 Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 10, 2026 at 11:03 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads While the San Francisco 49ers made a fairly mild move, the Dallas Cowboys didn't move the needle at the trade deadline. But these teams meet in Week 10 of the NFL season, and here are bold predictions for the contest. Entering with a record of 7-1, the 49ers sit as the No. 1 in the NFC. Meanwhile, the Cowboys are trying to fight their way back into contention in the NFC East. They have a record of 4-5. The 49ers are road favorites, but only by 3.5 points. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) 49ers QB Brock Purdy will throw for 250 yards and two TD passes It's a matter of scheme that Purdy will have success , according to ESPN. "Kyle Shanahan will have answers for both the run and pass game Sunday in Dallas," Matt Bowen wrote. "Schemed throws for Brock Purdy that create open coverage voids off play-action, plus a multiple run game with Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black to attack a Cowboys defense, allowing 5.0 YPC (third most). I like the 49ers to cover on the road." Purdy has thrown for 1,980 yards this season with 17 touchdowns and five interceptions. He has been impressive and has the eye of head coach Kyle Shanahan, according to a post on X by 95.7 TheGame via Heavy.com. "Yeah, it's been amazing," Shanahan said. "Just since the first game he got in there. That's why I struggle at the beginning of the year when everyone's asking me, can I believe how good he's playing and how much better he's improved because he was so good off the bench versus Miami in his first game and the second week… taking us to the NFC Championship as a rookie. "And I think his second year took us to the Super Bowl maybe. So Brock's been the man since he's come in, and it's pretty unbelievable deal considering where he was drafted, how he started… very fortunate to have Brock." The Cowboys will have their hands full. Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb will get 8-plus catches and 90-plus yards The Cowboys are going to get the ball to Lamb. It's their best path to having a shot at beating the 49ers. Lamb left the win over the Colts with a sigh of relief, according to dallascowboys.com. "Those are the games that you love to end up on top," Lamb said. "We understand it was the same situation that we were kind of in last week, and we didn't end up on top then, so just finishing out the game, finishing out the drive — shout out to the defense for ending the game. "But I think I had, like, three penalties alone in the second half, and a fumble. Personally, I gotta take a real good look. The numbers look crazy, but it could have been more. And I'm always thinking about what could have been. So, as for me, as a leader on this offense,I feel like I've got to be better in some realms and just end the game." The 49ers are off to a great start. But before the season, the Cowboys were in the same conversation with them. Lamb said the Cowboys need to get the job done. "We know what we got going on, just the history of that [matchup], the guys that they have over there on defense and the prep, I mean, it's going to take a lot of a lot of preparation, and a lot of execution," Lamb said. "We can't have as many flags because they have a really good offense, too." Prescott will lean heavily on Lamb if George Pickens misses another game. But even if Pickens plays, Prescott won't forget who he needs to target, early and often. 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey will get in the end zone twice Look for McCaffrey to score on the ground and with a reception. The 49ers are going to get him the ball near the goal line. One thing that helps McCaffrey's overall usage is that Shanahan is more confident that he is ready to rock after a pre-bye injury slowed him somewhat, according to ninerswire.com. "No. I actually forgot about it," Shanahan said. "He had a good bye week, and he told me before the bye week in Christian style not to worry about it at all. He'll be fine, and he looked good all week." McCaffrey hasn't had a blowout game all season. His rushing high is 75 yards, and his receiving high is 61. But he has 10 total touchdowns, with nine of them coming off the ground. And consistency has been a hallmark. McCaffrey has scored in seven straight games. In three of those contests, he scored twice. The 49ers will need to be sharp offensively. Despite the way their defense has played, they will have trouble slowing down the Cowboys' high-octane offense. McCaffrey will likely need those scores to keep his team in good business. Fourteen penalties will do that. The Cowboys can move the ball against the 49ers, especially if George Pickens' hamstring cooperates and the visitors are still banged up in the secondary. I have a much harder time seeing Dallas get enough stops. Christian McCaffrey scored on the ground and through the air last week, and San Francisco ran for 190 yards to blitz Las Vegas. If Dallas has to commit extra help to stop McCaffrey, Brock Purdy will have openings downfield – maybe even in the form of new toy Keenan Allen. The Cowboys are capable of hanging around at home. They won't win. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: 49ers 28, Cowboys 16 Closing out games has been a problem for Dallas this season. That might not come into factor here ... But only because San Francisco could run away with this one. Even a shorthanded version of the 49ers offense should be able to push Christian Parker's defense into uncomfortable positions. Meanwhile, Brian Schottenheimer's attack could be in for a tough day if it hits any more cold stretches. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: 49ers 34, Cowboys 23 The 49ers are just in a different class, even with the injuries. Kyle Shanahan should have his way with this Dallas defense, which barely scraped by the lowly Colts last week. When things are going right, the Cowboys light up the scoreboard – except nothing has gone right this season. It's hard to believe a step up in competition is going to do the Cowboys any favors against a 49ers team that just added some reinforcements at the trade deadline to prepare for a long playoff run. home.headline: NFL Fans Question Cowboys CB Joey Porter Jr.’s Concerning Injury Disclosure
home.blurb: “My goal is to win games and play football and that’s what I want to do,” he said in comments shared by the Cowboys . He denied that his contract was behind the absence and said he had resumed running, although that did not guarantee a return against San Francisco. Joey Porter Jr. offered a blunt assessment of his injured foot. The responses were every bit as blunt. The Dallas Cowboys cornerback says his condition worsened while he tried to play through it. That explanation did little to quiet fans questioning his availability, with some dragging his contract situation into the discussion. Porter has directly rejected that connection. Joey Porter Jr.’s Injury Update Draws Harsh Reactions Porter told NFL Network’s Jane Slater that “the whole foot is jacked up,” according to her account of their conversation . He said the problem began against Houston and worsened as he continued to play. His explanation centered on the movement required to cover receivers. Without being able to run and change direction properly, he felt he could become a liability. Several fans were already convinced something else was going on. “Pittsburgh Steelers front office is laughing their [expletive] off. They fleeced the Cowboys…this guy doesn’t want to play,” one fan wrote . “Don’t believe anything he says. His agent is running this show,” another added . Those accusations go beyond what Porter has disclosed about his injury. Still, the frustration over his availability came through loud and clear. “Always hurt and whines a lot… let’s get rid of him and many others,” one fan said . Another response pulled fellow former Steeler George Pickens into the criticism. “Feel bad for Dallas fans as they are as dedicated and passionate as us yinzers. But Pickens and JPJ are both frauds — great talent but not worth the drama,” the fan wrote . SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer Dallas has had plenty of frustration to go around, including DeMarvion Overshown’s penalty while inactive against Indianapolis . Porter’s update gave an already irritated audience another subject to argue about. Porter Pushes Back Against Contract Speculation The money conversation followed Porter into the replies, too. “That 28 mil AVV from the Steelers is gonna be the best offer that dude will ever see,” one fan wrote . The $28 million annual figure was supported by reporting on Pittsburgh’s offer, though the structure of the guarantees was a major sticking point. Other commenters focused on guaranteed money and whether Porter wanted to play without a new deal. “THIS is why the guaranteed $ means soooo much to him. He’s soft and ALWAYS hurt,” another fan posted . “He stinks — soft and doesn’t want to play without a contract. He turned down the best deal he was going to get,” one user on X wrote . “A tale as old as time. The boy who cried wolf. Good luck in free agency!” another added . Porter’s own explanation directly disputes those theories. Dallas could certainly use the help. The C

Porter did not practice Wednesday or Thursday, according to the Cowboys’ official injury report. On Thursday, he said his whole foot was “jacked up,” but he said he hoped to run and cut Friday and play Sunday. “Get him out there, let him move around a little bit, see how he does, and again, hope to get a little bit more from him today,” Schottenheimer explained. “I know he’s trying everything in his power to get back and get ready to roll.” Ravens reveal Lamar Jackson recovering from broken and dislocated thumb, out 'about 6-10 weeks' Chiefs' Kenneth Walker listed as questionable against Falcons after late injury report addition Entertainment Entertainment Home ··· Boxing FRISCO, Texas — Dallas Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. has missed two straight practices with an ankle injury, and Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said Friday that Porter can play against the San Francisco 49ers without a practice this week. Schottenheimer spoke before Friday’s practice at The Star in a press conference the Cowboys streamed on YouTube . Friday’s final injury report, with game designations for Sunday, comes after practice and after Schottenheimer’s availability. He’s got a great feel for that, but most importantly is let’s see how he moves around today. But the answer to the question is yes.” Schottenheimer Sets Friday Test For Joey Porter Jr. The Cowboys planned to put Porter on the field Friday to see how he handles more work, and Schottenheimer said Porter is pushing to be ready. A final answer may not come until Saturday. Schottenheimer called Friday a big day for teams around the league, including San Francisco, as they evaluate their players. “Could be, could be,” Schottenheimer said. “Again, Friday is a big day for everybody around the National Football League. home.headline: Cowboys Reportedly Sign New RB After 2026 NFL Trade Deadline, Tyler Goodson Injury
home.blurb: The TCU product was available because the New Orleans Saints released him after he appeared in six games for the NFC South team this season. He ran for 159 yards and two touchdowns on an ugly 2.8 yards per carry in those six games. Dallas Cowboys fans may have been hoping for a more consequential move ahead of Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET NFL trade deadline, but they reportedly did make a running back addition. Calvin Watkins of the Dallas Morning News reported the Cowboys signed Kendre Miller to its practice squad with Tyler Goodson dealing with a knee injury he suffered in Sunday's win over the Indianapolis Colts. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters Monday that Goodson will miss "multiple weeks" with the setback. Cowboys Had No Pickens Trade Calls Report: Pickens Had No Trade Market The timing was less than ideal for Goodson, as he was just starting to establish himself in the running back rotation behind Javonte Williams. He finished with a season-high 12 carries for 77 yards in the win over the Colts, which marked his second time in a three-game span with double-digit carries. Yet his injury put the team in scramble mode as it attempted to find another backup for Williams. ▶️ Full Cowboys-Colts Recap 04:46 Enter Miller, whom ESPN's Todd Archer reported visited with the Cowboys on Tuesday before their decision to sign him. Miller was also an occasional threat in the Saints' passing game with nine catches on a career-high 13 targets this season. While he isn't someone who is going to carry the offense on his back, the Cowboys won't ask him to do so. Instead, he will surely be put in a role where he is expected to fill in for Williams on a handful of series throughout games to keep the starter fresher for the stretch run. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Imagn Images Week 10 in the NFL is here, and it's the first week where all the players who were dealt at the trade deadline will make their debuts with their new teams. Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings , the Jacksonville Jaguars traded for three new defensive players, including Jordan Davis , and the Kansas City Chiefs gave Patrick Mahomes a new wideout in Josh Downs . Which one of these additions will be most beneficial for a Super Bowl run? This Sunday, the New England Patriots and Detroit Lions will battle in Germany, the Vikings and Green Bay Packers play an important divisional matchup and the Cincinnati Bengals look to steal the AFC North lead from the Pittsburgh Steelers . Which teams should you pick in Week 10, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 11 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research New England Patriots vs. Detroit Lions (-2.5) (Munich) Dajani (Lions -2.5): It's going to take me some time to get over watching the Patriots have 45 points dropped on their face by the Packers. Drake Maye threw three interceptions, and the team could now be down its top two running backs. Rhamondre Stevenson is reportedly dealing with a knee injury, while TreVeyon Henderson experienced an " unusual medical emergency ." That leaves the Patriots with Corey Kiner and Lan Larison at running back. When it comes to the Lions, the question has never been about Jared Goff 's offense but about Kelvin Sheppard 's defense. No one is talking about it, but this unit has been better in recent weeks. In fact, over this four-game win streak, they rank second in points allowed per game (15.5) and yards allowed per game (286.3). Give me the Lions. … Prediction: Lions 28, Patriots 20 Dubin (Lions -2.5): The Patriots' rapidly thinning skill-position corps gives me some doubt that they can compete with the Lions offensively. Especially after New England's secondary was just lit up by the Packers, I can see Detroit having some passing game success here, bouncing back from a slow last two weeks through the air. And then Jahmyr Gibbs is always liable to go off. Drake Maye is capable of single-handedly carrying an offense against a bad defense, but as Dajani said, Detroit's defense has been playing better as of late. … Prediction: Lions 30, Patriots 21 Kansas City Chiefs (-3.5) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Chiefs -3.5): I initially wanted to take the points here with the Atlanta Falcons , but they just got home from Madrid and sent safety Jessie Bates III to the Jaguars at the trade deadline. The Falcons were dominated by the Bengals abroad, 34-17, meaning they have lost back-to-back games by at least 16 points. The Falcons' run defense will have to be ready for Kenneth Walker III , but I think the key to not getting caught by the hook could be Josh Downs, who the Chiefs acquired this week at the trade deadline. He's not some downfield perimeter threat, but is a slot weapon that could spark Patrick Mahomes' passing game. … Prediction: Chiefs 26, Falcons 21 Dubin (Chiefs -3.5): Atlanta has been getting clobbered on the ground lately (123 or more rushing yards allowed in four of the last five games and 200 or more twice) and is about to run into the Kenneth Walker train. The Chiefs finally added someone who can beat man coverage in Josh Downs, and while it might take him a few weeks to get fully up to speed, he should help them immediately in situational football. Plus, the Chiefs' defense has been really good against both the run and the pass. This line seems several points too low. … Prediction: Chiefs 27, Falcons 16 Minnesota Vikings at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Dajani (Vikings +3.5): I don't know how much time Kirk Cousins is going to need to get acclimated to his (somewhat) new situation in Minnesota, but I bet this organization and this defense are JUICED to add him to the fold. Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz simply weren't cutting it, and Cousins has actually been playing some good ball out in Vegas. His 20 passing touchdowns rank second in the NFL, and his 260.0 passing yards per game rank eighth. Cousins also has chemistry with Justin Jefferson , whose 98.9 receiving yards per game when catching passes from Cousins are the most by a QB-WR duo all-time. This Packers passing attack has been lethal with Jordan Love playing MVP football and Christian Watson and Matthew Golden looking like prime Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle , but give me the Vikings to keep it close. … Prediction: Packers 20, Vikings 17 Dubin (Vikings +3.5): In-division rematches are typically lower scoring than the first matchup, so like Dajani, I see a fairly low-scoring game here despite the fact that the Packers' offense has been a fireworks show and the Vikings just upgraded their quarterback situation. These two defenses are playing extraordinarily well right now, and I think they'll be able to get a handle on what each offense is doing. In the end, I trust Jordan Love more than I do Kirk Cousins, so we'll take the Packers in a close, low-scoring game. … Prediction: Packers 17, Vikings 14 San Francisco 49ers (-3.5) at Dallas Cowboys Dajani ( 49ers -3.5): This is historically a great rivalry, but this year it's the Super Bowl favorite vs. a team that struggles with everyone they play. The 49ers have the most games missed due to injury this season (159), but that hasn't stopped them from starting 7-1. Brock Purdy 's offense scores touchdowns on 37.2% of its drives, which is the fifth-highest rate by any team since 2000! Last week's win against the Las Vegas Raiders showed how well-rounded the 49ers are, as they scored two passing touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and a defensive touchdown. … Prediction: 49ers 30, Cowboys 26 Dubin (49ers -3.5): I don't care how many skill-position players the 49ers are missing or how old the ones that are actually healthy are: Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy are going to cut through this Dallas defense like a hot knife through butter. The Niners are so efficient on a per-play basis both on the ground and through the air, and the Cowboys make even bad offenses look competent. Dallas might be able to get something going on its side of the ball, especially if George Pickens returns to the lineup, but I don't expect it to be nearly enough to compete with what San Francisco does on offense. … Prediction: 49ers 34, Cowboys 23 Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals (-3.5) (SNF) Dajani (Bengals -3.5): I'll keep saying it, this may be Joe Burrow 's year to win MVP. He's accounted for 26 total touchdowns through eight games, while Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have combined for 47 receptions, 693 yards and eight touchdowns just over the last three games. The Bengals have scored 34 points in three straight games and 30 points in four straight games. The Steelers defeated the Bengals in Pittsburgh in Week 3, 30-27, but the Bengals will even the series on Sunday night. Cincy is 7-2 SU and ATS in its last nine home primetime games. … Prediction: Bengals 30, Steelers 24 Dubin (Steelers +3.5): I'm taking the Bengals to win, but I like the Steelers to keep things uncomfortably close. Pittsburgh always seems to be right in the thick of it in these division games, and the first matchup was decided by only three points. I think the scoring margin is the same here, but with slightly lower scoring, in keeping with the trend of divisional rematches. … Prediction: Bengals 23, Steelers 20 Los Angeles Chargers at Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) (MNF) Dajani ( Chargers +4.5): This is potentially the worst Monday night game of all time. A winless team that hasn't covered the spread since last year vs. a spiraling team starting a new quarterback. Jacoby Brissett is an upgrade over Joe Fagnano , but how much of an upgrade immediately? I don't have a great read on this matchup, but I'll take Jim Harbaugh to keep things close with his brother's old team. … Prediction: Ravens 20, Chargers 17 Dubin (Chargers +4.5): I don't feel good at all about predicting the Chargers to actually keep a game close, but that's what I'm going to do here. I'm not going as far as predicting that they'll get their first win, but I think they can hang in the game against Jacoby Brissett in his first start with Baltimore. The Ravens' offense should be better than it was with Joe Fagnano under center, but I'm not sure it will fully hit the ground running right away. LA's offense is pretty broken, but the Ravens haven't exactly been great defensively (25th in scoring defense), so the Chargers might be able to put at least some points on the board. … Prediction: Ravens 24, Chargers 20 Washington Commanders at New York Giants (-2.5) (TNF) Da

Not to mention, these two teams have already played this season. It was in Week 3, with the Steelers winning 30-27 in Pittsburgh. Right now on FanDuel , the Bengals are 3.5-point favorites next Sunday night. The Bengals' moneyline is -200, while the Steelers' is at +168. The over/under is at 47.5. Sunday night could be an extremely physical game. It's an AFC North rivalry with sole possession of first place in the division at stake. Also, it's the Bengals and Steelers. That's all you need to know for the potential level of physicality. Pittsburgh stole the first game against the Bengals, aided by two Bengals turnovers in the fourth quarter that included Joe Burrow getting strip-sacked with the Bengals on the edge of field goal range in the final minute. The Bengals never ran an offensive play with the lead in that game, but there were some great performances from their star players. Joe Burrow was 28/37 for 282 yards and three touchdowns, Ja'Marr Chase caught nine passes for 98 yards and a touchdown, and Tee Higgins hauled in six passes for 90 yards and a touchdown. Mike Gesicki also caught a 25-yard touchdown on 4th&2 early in the fourth quarter. For the Steelers, Aaron Rodgers completed 19 of 34 passes for 292 yards and three touchdowns, while Jaylen Warren rushed for 127 yards on 17 carries. Eight different players caught a pass for the Steelers, with Darnell Washington leading the way with 67 receiving yards on three receptions. Roman Wilson, D.K. Metcalf, and Ben Skowronek each caught a touchdown for the Steelers. Rodgers currently has 1,871 passing yards and 13 touchdowns on the season, but he's also thrown six interceptions and is completing just 60.8 percent of his passes. Warren has 704 rushing yards and two touchdowns, while Washington and fellow tight end Pat Friermuth lead the Steelers with three and four touchdowns, respectively. T.J. Watt, as of Sunday night, leads the NFL with 7.5 sacks, and he also has nine tackles for loss. Cornerback Jamel Dean also has three forced fumbles. Bengals right tackle Amarius Mims held T.J. Watt off the stat sheet in that game, which bodes well going into Sunday night. The Bengals' offense scored on five of their eight drives in the first meeting in Week 3, gaining 352 yards of offense and rushing for 83 yards on 18 carries. Chase Brown rushed for 61 yards on 13 carries.

In his last four games against the Steelers, Burrow has thrown 11 touchdowns and four interceptions, topping 275 yards in all four games. Interestingly, Pittsburgh is a great matchup for Burrow. The Steelers play zone coverage on 84.3% of dropbacks, according to Next Gen Stats, and Burrow is the best quarterback in the NFL against zone by completion percentage, at 74.7%. Jaylen Warren rushes for 120-plus yards Warren has become one of the league's most productive running backs this season, ranking sixth in rushing yards and first in yards per carry, at 5.9. Earlier this season against the Bengals , Warren ran for the second-most yards of his season, with 127. Two weeks ago against Cleveland, Warren topped that number with 143 yards. It was the first time all season he rushed for 100 yards in back-to-back games. The Bengals' defense has been inconsistent this season, struggling with tackling some weeks and shutting down opposing offenses and forcing takeaways in others. I think that, coming off a bye, the Steelers catch the Bengals on their back foot and feed Warren, who will have a big game. Steelers win 34-31 History is not on the Bengals' side in this matchup. After playing an overseas game, teams are 0-5 when their next game comes against a team coming off a bye. The Steelers are rested, while the Bengals are recovering from nearly a full week in Madrid. A lot is at stake in this game, with the winner taking sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Pittsburgh doesn't have much momentum, especially on offense, as its best wide receiver, DK Metcalf, has been struggling with drops lately. He has just 378 receiving yards this season and has topped 100 yards just once, with a 115-yard day against Cleveland earlier this season. Metcalf had just one catch for 4 yards on six targets against the Browns. The Steelers hit a snag at the right time, giving themselves a week to figure things out. I think the Steelers pick up a big win, halting the Bengals' momentum and getting a massive tiebreaker. Pittsburgh has done a relatively good job of keeping a cap on Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins over the last couple of seasons. Outside of Chase's massive 16-catch, 161-yard game with Joe Flacco at quarterback last season, neither has topped 100 yards in their last four meetings.

The former Steelers head coach knows exactly what this rivalry means after spending 19 years in Pittsburgh before stepping away from the role. He will now get to watch his old team from the NBC crew as the two sides prepare to meet on Sunday Night Football. Both teams enter the contest with 6-2 records and four consecutive victories, setting up a major meeting between two sides looking to strengthen their position in the AFC North. Mike Tomlin backs Steelers pass rush to challenge Joe Burrow and Cincinnati Bengals Tomlin made no secret of his excitement when discussing the matchup, admitting he would be more than happy to make the trip to Cincinnati. "It's AFC North football and you know I love that. You can airmail me right to Cincinnati," Tomlin said. He also highlighted the individual battle that could define the game, with Joe Burrow and the Bengals passing attack facing Pittsburgh's formidable pass rush. "It's good on good. Joe Burrow and that Cincinnati passing game vs T.J. Watt and the four-man rush of the Steelers…. Bring your popcorn and get your cameras ready." Pittsburgh will arrive with plenty of confidence after enjoying a bye week. The Steelers' four-game winning run includes a commanding 27-6 victory over the Cleveland Browns in their most recent outing. Cincinnati have also found their rhythm, beating the Atlanta Falcons 34-17 in Madrid. Burrow completed 82.8 per cent of his passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in that victory. However, the Bengals will have revenge on their minds after losing 30-27 to Pittsburgh during their earlier meeting this season. That defeat came during a difficult spell in which Cincinnati also suffered a second consecutive loss. Now, with both teams level at 6-2, the stakes are considerably higher. Tomlin will have a particularly interesting perspective from the NBC booth as he watches the Steelers take on a Bengals team that will be determined to settle the score on home turf. (Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images) | Getty Images Frank Platko · SB Nation Thu, November 12, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Updated Standings: Pittsburgh Steelers 6-2 Cincinnati Bengals 6-2 Cleveland Browns 5-4 Baltimore Ravens 4-5 Matchup: vs. Pittsburgh Steelers, 8:20pm EST The Bengals avoided a potential letdown game last week against the Atlanta Falcons in Spain, securing a 34-17 victory. After losing the first quarter by three points, the Bengals outscored the Falcons by 20 points for the remainder of the contest. Now riding a four-game win streak, having exceeded 30+ points in each game, the Bengals will return home for a primetime matchup with the Steelers. In Week 3, the Bengals suffered a 30-27 defeat against Pittsburgh and sit in second place now despite having the same record. Cincinnati's passing attack has been firing on all cylinders recently and Joe Burrow is hitting his stride. Over the last four games, Burrow has 16 touchdown passes while averaging over 300 passing yards. The Steelers are a Top 3 defense against the run but rank middle-of-the-pack defending the pass. The Bengals continue to struggle running the ball effectively, so they'll likely attack Pittsburgh's secondary regularly. Elsewhere, the Bengals' inconsistent run defense may be tested by Steelers' rushing attack that has totaled 148 yards and 200 yards on the ground in back-to-back games. The Bengals will need to slow down Jaylen Warren in the backfield, who has been a star this season. If the Bengals can make the Steelers one dimensional offensively, they become a much more beatable team. Matchup: vs. Cincinnati Bengals, 8:20pm EST Like their divisional counterpart, the Steelers have won their last four games to improve to 6-2, sitting atop the division by virtue of tiebreaker. Prior to last week's bye break, the Steelers defeated the Browns handedly by 21 points, their most lopsided win of the season and only their second win by more than one possession. Pittsburgh's momentum will be put to the test in a tough road environment this Sunday night with the AFC North lead on the line. The Steelers have won the turnover battle in three consecutive games. That will be an important factor for them to defeat the Bengals. Burrow has taken good care of the ball this year but did have a three-interception performance just two weeks ago. If the Steelers' defense can force a turnover or two and give their offense support with shorter fields, that will go a long way in helping them keep pace. On offense, the Steelers continue to long for better production from their pass-catchers to help unlock more downfield plays. Warren has been the team's only consistent playmaker and Rico Dowdle has ran well over the last two weeks in a complimentary role. However, D.K. Metcalf and company have been up-and-down in the passing game. In order to match Cincinnati's high-flying offensive attack, the Steelers will likely need to hit on a few explosive passing plays. Matchup: vs. Houston Texans, 1:00pm EST The Browns have now lost back-to-back games and are looking to get back on track before their upcoming bye week. In Week 9, they allowed a winnable game to slip through their grasp against the Saints, where they lost by one point in overtime. Shedeur Sanders impressed in his spot-start for Deshaun Watson at quarterback, but the Browns still struggled to run the ball and didn't start scoring much until the fourth quarter. Watson is set to return from injury to start this week versus his former team. The Texans have underwhelmed defensively this year but still have one of the league's more talented defenses, which will pose a challenge for the Browns — whose offense has struggled mightily at times this season. Houston has been vulnerable in pass coverage, allowing over 235 passing yards per game, leaving some hope that Watson can hit a downfield shot or two. The Browns will need to connect on some type of explosive plays or find a way to run the ball more effectively. Defensively, the Browns will need to bring their A game, as the Texans have prolific offensively at times in recent weeks. Last Sunday, they scored 44 points and C.J. Stroud threw five touchdown passes with nearly 400 passing yards. The Browns may be able to afford to sell out against the pass rather than the run, as the Texans rank even worse running the ball than they do. Matchup: vs. Los Angeles Chargers, 8:15pm EST The Ravens were thrashed by the Jacksonville Jaguars last Thursday night, losing by 20+ points for the third straight game. Baltimore's offense struggles hit a new low, as the team scored 10 points, gained 10 first downs and totaled just over 200 yards. With a hobbled third-string quarterback under center, the Ravens were no match for a talented Jaguars' squad. Fortunately, they will get the ultimate potential get-right matchup this coming Monday, taking on a winless Chargers team that is in disarray. Hopes for a potential offensive turnaround lie with new incoming quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who the Ravens traded for after Week 9. Brissett should provide a significant upgrade over Joe Fagnano as an experienced veteran who has proven, at the bare minimum, he can lead scoring drives and operate an offense at a competent level. Even with Brissett now under center, the Ravens need more consistency from their offensive line and breakthrough performances from veterans like Mark Andrews, Ronnie Stanley and Derrick Henry. Defensively, the Ravens have given up 30+ points in three straight weeks to three of the best offenses and quarterbacks in the NFL. They've played good halves and quarters, but the lows have been low. Coverage breakdowns and lack of impact pass rush continue to plague them. If there were ever a spot to have a convincing performance and force turnovers, this would be it. Chargers' quarterback Justin Herbert leads all quarterbacks in interceptions this season.

picks.headline: Steelers vs Bengals Week 10 Preview: Pittsburgh Must Slow Down Cincinnati Offense

It's official: Poch to Man United Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Drew VonScio, Editor Drew VonScio, Editor · Last Word on Sports Fri, November 13, 2026 at 4:26 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers know a lot is on the line in Sunday night's AFC North matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals, as the winner controls their own destiny for the division title. The Steelers found a way to win in an offensive shootout in Week 3 , but that style of play is unlikely to work again. This Steelers vs. Bengals matchup is going to come down to how well Pittsburgh can run the football, and more importantly, how the defense can slow down Joe Burrow and the best passing offense in the league. Steelers vs Bengals Week 10 Preview: Do Whatever It Takes to Stop Joe Burrow Stopping or slowing down Cincinnati's offense is easier said than done. Burrow is leading a pass offense that averages 285 yards through the air per game, and Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are without a doubt the best receiving duo in the NFL. That duo accounted for 187 yards and three touchdowns against the Atlanta Falcons . In Sunday's Steelers vs. Bengals matchup, that simply can't happen. Steelers wide receiver D.K. Metcalf has just as much faith in the defense as he does those in the offensive huddle with him. "Two good offenses going against each other, so I think, as I said, the best defensive team is going to win the game," Metcalf told Greg Mcafee of DK Pittsburgh Sports on Thursday . "I think we're going to put up a lot of points. They're going to put up a lot of points if they can get past our defense. But the way our defense is playing, it's going to be tough for them to do that." One of the best ways for the Steelers to slow down Burrow and the Bengals offense is something that Patrick Graham already utilizes with a lot of zone coverage. Pittsburgh needs as many members of the secondary downfield as possible to limit Chase and Higgins. If Burrow and Zac Taylor want to try beating the Steelers by dinking and dumping it to Chase Brown and Mike Gesicki, the Steelers will take their chances. This Steelers vs. Bengals matchup may see the return of defensive tackle Derrick Harmon. Harmon left midway through the second quarter against the Cleveland Browns and hasn't played since. Even with only rushing four, Harmon would give the defense a much-needed boost if he is able to play. "It just adds to our rotation [of defensive linemen] and allows us to be interchangeable," Cam Heyward told Jose Negron of DK Pittsburgh Sports on Wednesday . "It should pay dividends on Sunday." Steelers vs Bengals Matchup May See the Debut of White Chocolate The wide receiver room is still a concern for Pittsburgh with Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr. still on injured reserve. General manager Omar Khan chose not to add anyone at the trade deadline, and Steelers fans were less than thrilled. However, this Steelers vs. Bengals matchup could see White Chocolate make an impact. White Chocolate, known outside of the locker room as Max Hurleman, has been on the practice squad since the beginning of the season. If the Steelers had multiple wide receivers injured in August, he may have even made the 53-man roster. As a fellow receiver, Metcalf and head coach Mike McCarthy know what Hurleman can bring to the table. "Yeah, White Chocolate," Metcalf clarified to Chris Adamski of TribLive on Thursday . "He makes plays; he's going to go out there and make plays. He made plays in camp." "How do you not love Max? Max is one of the guys… who comes in every day and works hard," McCarthy mentioned to Adamski in his press briefing on Thursday . "The GPS [data], he rips that up." The Last Word: Steelers vs Bengals Will Require All 60 Minutes Make no mistake about it: Steelers vs. Bengals Sunday night is going to be a grind. Pittsburgh is going to have to play some of its best football of the season on the road in Cincinnati. The Bengals know they were one possession away from winning the early-season meeting between these two teams and will use that as motivation on Sunday night. Slowing down Burrow will be difficult, but the defense knows exactly what it needs to do to be successful. Graham has been phenomenal for the Steelers since moving down to the sidelines, and he is pushing all of the right buttons. And on a night where the Steelers will be in dark uniforms, White Chocolate may also prove to be a difference maker. Fortunately, Monday night's matchup against the Baltimore Ravens could be one of their best chances to finally get into the win column. Baltimore is dealing with major injuries, including the absence of Lamar Jackson, and will turn to newly acquired quarterback Jacoby Brissett . The Ravens are also struggling to find consistency at 4-5. Meanwhile, the Chargers are coming off another ugly loss after allowing C.J. Stroud to throw for 384 yards and five touchdowns. Could Jim Harbaugh finally get his team a victory? Here are three bold predictions for Chargers-Ravens on Monday Night Football. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Bold Prediction No. 3: Jacoby Brissett throws for 2+ touchdowns in Ravens debut Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Brissett is now a Raven, and his first start with Baltimore will come at home against the Chargers . Los Angeles has a solid defense and typically does a good job making life difficult for opposing quarterbacks. However, that certainly wasn't the case against Houston. Stroud walked all over the Chargers on Sunday, throwing for 384 yards and five touchdowns. Brissett isn't the same kind of quarterback, but he has plenty of NFL experience and should have enough weapons around him to make an impact in his first game with Baltimore. I expect at least two of his passes to find the end zone Monday night. Zay Flowers could be in line for a productive performance, which would be welcome news for fantasy managers who have been waiting for the Ravens' offense to get back on track. Bold Prediction No. 2: Keaton Mitchell scores a touchdown against his former team This is probably the boldest prediction of the three. Mitchell will face his former team for the first time since joining the Chargers, and I think he'll find a way to make his return memorable. Mitchell has one touchdown this season, and it came through the air. He's recorded 46 carries for 178 yards, averaging 3.9 yards per attempt, while adding 18 receptions for 103 yards. The Chargers have continued to rotate their running backs, making it difficult to predict which player will receive the most opportunities. However, Mitchell has shown that he can contribute as both a runner and receiver. In primetime, I expect him to get a chance near the goal line and take advantage of it. Scoring against the team that gave him his NFL opportunity would make for a pretty good Monday night story. Bold Prediction No. 1: The Chargers win their first game of the 2026 season The Chargers have a chance to win? Yes, they do. Without Lamar Jackson under center, Baltimore is a much more vulnerable opponent. The Ravens are 4-5, dealing with injuries and trying to get their season back on track. Meanwhile, the Chargers are desperate to avoid falling to 0-9. There's also an interesting storyline on the sideline. Jesse Minter , who previously served as the Chargers' defensive coordinator, will face his former boss, Jim Harbaugh, for the first time as opposing head coaches. Harbaugh's first season in Los Angeles has been a disaster, but this is an opportunity to give his team something positive. Justin Herbert needs to play much better than he did against Houston, and I expect him to respond with a more competitive performance. Baltimore still has plenty of defensive talent. Marlon Humphrey and Roquan Smith could make things difficult for Herbert, while Kyle Hamilton would be another major factor if he's healthy enough to play. This could be an ugly game, with both offenses struggling to find consistency. However, I think the Chargers finally get over the hump and leave Baltimore with a victory. Score Prediction: Chargers win 20-17, with Cameron Dicker making four field goals. Los Angeles can't go 0-17, can it? picks.blurb: 2. Justin Herbert avoided a fracture: Now, can the Chargers protect him? Imaging came back negative on the middle finger of his non-throwing hand, and Herbert said he expects to play. The bigger matchup concern is that Houston sacked him a career-high eight times. Baltimore can make this a long night if the Chargers keep putting him in third-and-long. 3. Keep an eye on Kyle Hamilton's hip: If Baltimore's safety is limited or unavailable, that could give Herbert more room to attack the middle of the field with quick throws. That's one way for the Chargers to take pressure off their offensive line, especially if Ladd McConkey is healthy enough to handle his usual workload. 4. Something's gotta give: Right? Los Angeles is 0-8, the NFL's only remaining winless team. Baltimore has dropped four in a row to plummet to the bottom of the AFC North after a 4-1 start. Someone will win in primetime. Unless there's a tie. 5. Home is for the birds: Baltimore is 2-11 ATS at home since the start of last season, failing to cover by 9.7 points per game, according to Evan Abram's NFL betting primer. The Ravens have failed to cover the spread in eight straight home games, which is the longest home against-the-spread skid in franchise history. 6. Primetime Herbert: With Justin Herbert, the Chargers are 18-8 ATS in primetime night games, winning six in a row outright since 2024. Am I really going to change course now just because Lamar Jackson's unavailable? No chance. Jacoby Brissett will make his first Ravens start and it remains to be seen how good he'll be but he's absolutely an immediate upgrade on rookie Joe Fagnano and likely journeyman Tyler Huntley as well. Brissett's used to a heavy passing load and maybe that will bring Zay Flowers back to life. As for the Bolts, Justin Herbert plans to play after hurting a finger on his non-throwing hand. He just took eight sacks in Houston and Baltimore's defense is fully capable of frustrating him as well. Plus, Ladd McConkey still isn't right. This may not get ugly, but it won't end well for Los Angeles. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Chargers 17-16 Is it time? The Bolts finally ended their 37-possession touchdown drought last week, and maybe the long-sought first win could be in sight. That might seem like a stretch against most teams, but facing the floundering Ravens gives Los Angeles a chance for another breakthrough. Getting Jacoby Brissett in the fold might raise Baltimore's floor a bit, but this feels like another team that's fighting against its emerging reality of a lost season. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Chargers 20, Ravens 15 Maybe? Finally? There's a chance? Yes, the Chargers are going to finally win a football game this week. L.A. gets to take on old friend and current Ravens head coach Jesse Minter on 'Monday Night Football' in what might be one of the worst games of the season. The Ravens are down to Jacoby Brissett at quarterback, who is tasked with guiding an already uninspiring offense. The Chargers are desperate for a win and this isn't a Ravens defense to be worried about. The stars are aligning, even though we won't be seeing many on the field. The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-8 after falling to the Houston Texans at home in Week 9. Now the Chargers will have a chance to face off against the Baltimore Ravens on the road in Week 10’s edition of Monday Night Football. The the Ravens are fresh off a loss against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday Night Football, in which they started third-string rookie Joe Fagnano due to injuries plaguing Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley. The Ravens are expected to start Jacoby Brissett after acquiring him in a trade with the Arizona Cardinals for a fourth-round pick. The Chargers did end their long streak of not having a touchdown late in the fourth quarter, with wide receiver Quentin Johnston breaking off a 58-yard score. Still, there was not a lot to like from their 44-22 loss at home. The game against the Ravens will mark the team’s first game facing off against former defensive coordinator Jesse Minter, who became the Ravens’ head coach during the offseason. away.blurb: The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-7 and continue to shock the NFL world by showing an unwillingness to trade any of their players despite facing down a lost season in 2026. Los Angeles had hoped to right the ship and gain some momentum coming out of their week seven bye but looked listless against the Los Angeles Rams in week eight. game status for week 9 vs HOU DOUBTFUL — Kayode Awosika, David Njoku, Denzel Perryman, Brenen Thompson OUT — Deane Leonard, Kendall Williamson The Chargers do have other players who may be targets on the trade market but so far the word that has been put out to insiders around the NFL is that the Chargers are continuing to execute their plan of standing pat and trying to right the ship before heading into the 2027 season. The return of Donte Jackson to field is intriguing as he has been floated as a possible trade candidate and the Chargers have built up significant young depth both on the roster and the practice squad. Chargers Final Injury Report Before NFL Trade Deadline Skip to main content SI.COM The Chargers have been battered by injuries this season. The joke around the NFL may be about the San Francisco 49ers electrical substation and its proximity to the practice facility but someone may need to look into the water in Los Angeles with the amount of injuries both LA teams have faced this season. By week six, the Chargers had over half of their original 53-man roster either on that week's injury report or on injured reserve. The Chargers are already down to their fifth option at left guard and despite hope for getting reinforcements to face the Houston Texans, it appears guard Kayode Awosika, who has not played since week two, is still at least one week away from returning to the field. The Chargers opened the practice windows for tight end David Njoku and linebacker Denzel Perryman this week but it appears that neither are ready to be activated off of injured reserve just yet. The Chargers are set to get some depth at cornerback returning to the field with Donte Jackson and rookie Rodney Shelley clear of the injury report and will carry no injury designation into the game on Sunday. Chargers Injury Report: 9 players sit out 1st practice of Week 10 The Chargers began their prep for the Ravens with a whopping 18 players listed on their Thursday injury report. Of those players, over half of them sat out with a DNP tag. That group of nine included wide receiver Ladd McConkey (back), offensive guard/tackle Branson Taylor (ankle), defensive tackle Justin Eboigbe (ankle), and cornerback Isas Waxter (ankle). Every other player was given a limited designation. That group includes tight end David Njoku and linebacker Denzel Perryman, both of whom are likely to be activated this week off of IR. Offensive guard/tackle Trey Pipkins also had his practice window activated this week, although he did miss Thursday's practice altogether for personal reasons. Following the botched trade to the Broncos, linebacker Daiyan Henley was a DNP Thursday for personal reasons. Jim Harbaugh told reporters prior to practice that Henley got back to LA from Denver late Wednesday night and his attendance on Thursday was always going to be TBD. McConkey's injury continuing to keep him out of practice is worrisome. After being completely off the final injury report before the Texans game, he never made it onto the field as sudden back spasms kept him from playing. Now, four days later, those back spasms are still enough of a problem to keep him from practicing. This is most certainly something to monitor this week. home.blurb: "Recovery timelines are challenging to predict, but injuries like this that require surgery typically take about 6-10 weeks to heal," Minter said. "He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return." Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss between six and 10 weeks as he recovers from a broken and dislocated thumb, head coach Jesse Minter said in a statement on Friday. Jackson's health has been a primary storyline surrounding the Ravens throughout the 2026 campaign. First, he missed three games because of a high ankle sprain. While he returned for Baltimore's Week 8 game against the Buffalo Bills, he exited after his first snap with the thumb injury that required surgery. To make matters worse, Baltimore lost backup Tyler Huntley to a turf toe injury and had to turn to Joe Fagnano for the rest of the loss to the Bills and the entirety of the following loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Ravens scrambled and traded for Jacoby Brissett in an effort to weather the storm. Baltimore is looking to snap a four-game losing streak Monday night against the winless Los Angeles Chargers.

home.headline: Ravens get devastating update on Lamar Jackson’s status
home.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens offered a clearer picture of Lamar Jackson’s recovery Friday but stopped short of setting a return date for their franchise quarterback. “Recovery timelines are challenging to predict, but injuries like this that require surgery typically take about 6-10 weeks to heal. He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return.” Jackson injured his throwing hand on Baltimore’s first offensive play against Buffalo on November 1. His right hand struck Bills pass rusher Greg Rousseau as he attempted a throw, immediately ending his return to the lineup. He had already missed three games with an ankle injury. Related Articles Kirk Cousins’ Vikings Return Comes With an Emotional Twist In a statement released by the team, head coach Jesse Minter said injuries like Jackson’s broken and dislocated thumb typically require six to 10 weeks to heal when surgery is necessary. The update leaves Baltimore preparing for an extended stretch without the two-time NFL MVP as it tries to reverse a four-game losing streak. “Lamar is doing well as he recovers from the broken and dislocated thumb injury he suffered in Week 8,” Minter said. Minter described a typical healing window rather than announcing Jackson would miss another six to 10 weeks beginning Friday. The statement did not specify a target game or establish when that recovery window began. The Ravens’ quarterback problems worsened that afternoon when Tyler Huntley suffered a toe injury in the second quarter. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano finished the Buffalo game and started the following Thursday against Jacksonville. Baltimore lost those games 36-10 and 33-10, respectively, falling to 4-5. Following the loss, the Ravens made a trade to acquire Jacoby Brissett from Arizona on November 6. The veteran is preparing to make his first Baltimore start Monday night against the Los Angeles Chargers (0-8) while learning a new offense on an accelerated schedule. “It’s definitely a crash course. No question,” Brissett said Thursday. Baltimore has scored no more than 13 points in any game during its four-game skid. Brissett’s immediate assignment is to restore enough offensive consistency to stop that slide. Jackson has not abandoned the possibility of returning this season. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport previously reported that he told teammates he intended to come back, although his recovery and Baltimore’s ability to remain competitive will shape that possibility. The Ravens need to keep their season alive while Jackson recovers. That responsibility now falls to Brissett, whose first start Monday offers Baltimore a chance to end its four-game skid and give its injured quarterback something to come back to.
